entry.title: Bill Skarsgård Says He ‘Wasn’t Even Thrown Into the Mix’ to Be James Bond: ‘Maybe They Were Like, “We Can’t Do a Swede”’
entry.body: Bill Skarsgård won’t be the next 007, but he would play a Bond villain. In a recent appearance on Josh Horowitz’s “Happy Sad Confused” podcast, Skarsgård revealed he wasn’t asked to test for Denis Villeneuve’s reboot. “They didn’t call me about James Bond. I don’t know what that was about,” he joked. “Every single British, Australian [actor] … but maybe they were like, ‘We can’t do a Swede for this guy.’ I wasn’t even thrown into the mix.” Casting rumors for the new Bond have recently reached a fever pitch, with names like Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden swirling around. Most recently, Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult were revealed to have screen-tested for the role. Skarsgård agreed with Horowitz that he wouldn’t want to sign on for a decade plus of playing 007. “Just want to go in and do one Mads Mikkelsen villain.” “It’s not something that I’m actively looking for, but if I feel compelled to do something, yeah,” Skarsgård continued. A lot of people ask me, what goes into picking your roles or whatever and I don’t really know how to say it other than I feel drawn or compelled to. It’s something that you can’t really put your words on it and describe why it’s happening.” He added: “But I’ve also noticed that I don’t want to become jaded. Which means that I think I could probably go long stretches without working and waiting for something to be compelling enough for me to work on.” The Swedish actor is no stranger to a villainous character. He has played Pennywise in the “It” movies, Count Orlok in Robert Eggers’ “Nosferatu,” Eric Draven in “The Crow” and Marquis Vincent Bisset de Gramont in “John Wick: Chapter 4.” But he told Horowitz that he is becoming more discerning about the villain roles he takes on. “For a villain, it would have to be something that felt original to me, that was something that I hadn’t done before,” Skarsgård said. “I feel, kind of, spent with those things. But there are villains [that] could be really fun in different ways and if it’s the right kind.”

entry.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: It's Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie - Deadline
entry.body: Watch on Deadline A rep for Canadian streamer Crave said that there are no projects to confirm. Speculation that Heated Rivalry may be filming two seasons back-to-back has percolated for a while, fueled by a leaked August Cameo video by recurring guest star Dylan Walsh in which he said “I think we’re doing 12 [episodes] this time” before briefly writing in his profile that “a video went viral that got me in trouble.” Some interpreted his comments as Season 2 being supersized. Heated Rivalry creator Jacob Tierney last month debunked that theory, confirming to Andy Cohen that like Season 1, Season 2 will consist of 6 episodes. Neither he nor Crave have acknowledged a Season 3 pickup but Tierney said in the same SiriusXM interview with Cohen that they will be done filming by the end of the year without specifying what exactly the shoot covers. As for theatrical distribution, Heated Rivalry, which streams on HBO Max in the U.S. and several other key territories, has dabbled in that.

entry.title: ‘Full House’ Star Jodie Sweetin Says She Had ‘$190 in My Bank Account’ Before Filming ‘Fuller House’: ‘I Had to Borrow Money the First Week’
entry.body: Jodie Sweetin, who first shot to fame as Stephanie Tanner on the beloved sitcom “Full House,” is opening up about her financial struggles over the years, particularly how close she came to running out of funds before returning to the show’s 2016 reboot, “Fuller House.” “I had to borrow money the first week I was working on ‘Fuller House,’ and I [skittered] into my first paycheck with like $190 in my bank account,” Sweetin revealed on a recent episode of the “We’re Still Here, Babe” podcast. “And nobody that I worked with knew that.” Sweetin has been open about her struggles with addiction, and also discussed how those habits left her with “no money” at a certain point, leading her to broaden her employment search to non-Hollywood gigs. “I didn’t have [an] ego about it,” Sweetin said. “I didn’t care that I was, quote, unquote, working a normal job. I think other people again were like, ‘What are you doing here?’ And I was like, ‘Paying my bills. Kids don’t pay for themselves.’” She continued: “And not like I was ever a materialistic person, but you learn humility when you are at Target, and you’ve got to turn around and, you know, put some shit back, because you don’t have the money on your debit card.” “Full House” ran for eight seasons, from 1987 to 1995. “Fuller House” ran for five seasons on Netflix, totalling nearly 80 episodes. Original cast members, including Candace Cameron Bure, Andrea Barber, Scott Weinger, Bob Saget, Lori Loughlin, Dave Coulier and John Stamos, all returned for the series. (Notably absent were Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen.) Juan Pablo Di Pace, Adam Hagenbuch, John Brotherton, Michael Campion, Elias Harger and Soni Bringas also starred in the reboot.

entry.title: Trump says he asked Dana White, UFC boss, to be his new White House press secretary
entry.body: Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the president said in a social media post on Saturday. Trump described White, who staged a cage-fighting spectacle at the White House to mark the president’s 80th birthday in June, as “a violent Fighter and Warrior”, credentials unlike any ever used to describe previous press secretaries. Trump added that he asked White, a vocal supporter who campaigned for him in 2024, to bring six UFC fighters with him to serve as press aides. “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. “Dana, please take the job!” It was initially unclear whether the job offer was part of an actual plan, or an attention-grabbing stunt from a president desperate to change the subject from the huge losses suffered by his party in elections this week. There was no immediate response from White, who, some observers noted, might hesitate to leave a lucrative role running the UFC, which has earned him a fortune estimated to be in excess of $600m, for a job in government service that pays $195,000 a year. Later on Saturday, after CNN reported that White had declined the offer and that one aide to the president had described it as a joke, White posted an Instagram story with an image of himself in the White House briefing room above the caption: “On to the next chapter.” The UFC boss was then asked about the president’s post at a news conference after a boxing match in London on Saturday night. “I’m flying to Washington DC right now” to meet with Trump, White replied, without saying whether he would accept the job. “I’m going to meet with him, we have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that,” he added. The president’s Truth Social post was illustrated by seven images, including what appeared to be an AI-generated image of White behind the presidential seal in a press room, and photographs of the six UFC fighters whom Trump fantasizes about deploying to deal with reporters who ask him awkward questions: Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov (who are both from a Muslim-majority region of Russia), Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison – whose last name was mistakenly rendered as “Harris” by the president. In his post, Trump acknowledged that two of his dream hires, Makhachev and Nurmagomedov, are not Americans, but he did not mention that Nurmagomedov is reportedly close to the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, or that Makhachev has spoken out in defense of Palestinian civilians killed by Israel in Gaza. In 2023, Makhachev also celebrated a victory in one fight by saying, “Alhamdulillah,” the Arabic phrase for “praise be to God” used by Muslims. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was criticized in the rightwing media for using that same Arabic phrase in his victory speech this week. The first in a series of taxpayer-funded pro-Trump ads broadcast by the White House in the run-up to the recent midterms closed with images of the UFC fight on Trump’s birthday and remarks about him from White, who could be heard saying: “He is the toughest, most resilient human being I have ever met in my life.” White used that formulation to describe Trump multiple times during the 2024 presidential election campaign, most notably to sing Trump’s praises at the Republican national convention. The role of White House press secretary has been vacant for three weeks, since Trump’s previous pick, far-right commentator Katie Zacharia, was forced to resign after trying, and failing, to dodge questions about why she described herself as an attorney despite having failed the bar exam. Henry Smith contributed reporting

entry.title: How midterm elections sent Wall Street from celebration to mayhem in just 24 hours / this week - Yahoo Finance
entry.body: Wall Street's tumultuous midterm election week kicked off with a celebration among investors. On Wednesday, stocks soared after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress. The Dow (^DJI) surged more than 1,500 points. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) rallied nearly 2%. And in less than 24 hours, stocks reversed course, plunging Thursday as Wall Street and Main Street investors alike ditched artificial intelligence winners and chip stocks, sending the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) into correction territory. The extraordinary reversal marked just the latest whipsaw in a year of wild swings, with the market's best expectation of future volatility, the VIX (^VIX), spiking to its highest level since President Trump extended the deadline for the Iran war in late March. As the election results rolled in, Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, was glued to his television, flipping between CNN, Fox, MSNBC, and Bloomberg while watching stock futures slip. When Sosnick went to bed, futures were still down roughly 1%. Democrats had won control of both the House and Senate, resolving one major source of uncertainty for markets, while introducing a specific complication to the country's artificial intelligence investment boom. States where newly elected governors have promised to stop or pause data center construction account for an estimated 45% of planned US data center capacity, according to Goldman Sachs. In Texas, where more than half of the country's data center capacity is planned for construction, stakes were especially high. Democrat Gina Hinojosa had just won the race to become governor after promising a moratorium on new data center approvals. The shift caught the attention of one of the world's most prominent business titans. "Data centers in space look pretty appealing right now," Elon Musk posted on X early Wednesday. By Wednesday morning, Wall Street was seeing silver linings in the blue wave. The Dow jumped 3%, its best day in months. The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, and the Nasdaq gained 1.4%. Investors appeared to welcome the prospect of a divided government, potentially limiting some of President Trump's agenda. Oil prices (CL=F, BZ=F) also plunged, helping ease inflation concerns. And the removal of election uncertainty ushered in a sharp drop in the VIX. That drop may have encouraged volatility-sensitive trading strategies to buy stocks, adding more upward pressure to the rally, according to Sosnick. As prices climbed, more investors piled in. But beneath the rally, trouble was brewing.

entry.title: Anthropic IPO meets AI backlash after midterms show stinging rebuke of data centers - CNBC
entry.body: As concerns mounted, the debate over data centers intensified, while tech's hyperscalers simultaneously boosted their forecasts for capital expenditures, each reaching into the hundreds of billions of dollars. Anthropic and OpenAI depend on state-of-the-art data centers to train models and serve customers, and they're trying to build out capacity as quickly as possible to meet demand. Anthropic said in an amended IPO prospectus this week that it has entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements with an aggregate committed spend of about $895.4 billion, "substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure." Americans grappling with inflation and stubbornly high gas prices have grown worried that the facilities could exacerbate environmental harms, raise utility bills and contribute to job loss. For many, a proposed data center in their backyard became the physical manifestation of the widespread antipathy toward AI. In the risk factors section of its prospectus, Anthropic said opposition to data center development has become more organized across jurisdictions, and that the company's public profile could draw particular scrutiny to projects associated with it. Nicole Greene, an analyst at Gartner, said she expects that Anthropic's executives have long been prepared to contend with AI backlash, especially given the disruptive nature of the technology.

entry.title: Miami vs. Notre Dame live updates score: Follow the mega-matchup of old rivals in South Bend - Yahoo Sports
entry.body: Make that back-to-back touchdown drives for the Canes. Cooper Barkate's 12-yard catch caps the drive, and we've got a ballgame in South Bend. Notre Dame 24, Miami 17 A matchup of top-five teams in the AP Top 25 suddenly turned into a must-win game for Notre Dame with this week's College Football Playoff rankings reveal. 4 in the AP poll but found themselves on the outside of the top 10 in the CFP committee's eyes thanks to a schedule full of underwhelming opponents. 11 Notre Dame could really miss the College Football Playoff with a 10-2 record two years in a row. 1 Miami, Notre Dame will have to give QB CJ Carr some support with the run game. And opponents have found it very difficult to run on the Hurricanes. has emerged as Notre Dame's top rusher, while freshman Jonaz Walton is averaging nearly 7 yards a carry. Star CB Leonard Moore missed Notre Dame's win over Navy but should be ready to roll on Saturday night. His job becomes easier with the news that star Miami receiver Malachi Toney is out with an ankle injury suffered in practice. With Toney sidelined, Miami QB Darian Mensah is going to have to find his other receivers and lean on a run game that's been boosted by true freshman Javian Mallory. Follow along below for highlights and analysis on the game: Darian Mensah finds Elija Lofton in the end zone on an impressive toe-tapping catch. The Canes needed that one badly. Notre Dame 24, Miami 10 CJ Carr throws his third TD pass of the game, and his second to Micah Gilbert, who extends ND's lead with the 20-yard grab. Notre Dame 24, Miami 3 Miami QB Darian Mensah gets sacked by Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa on 3rd down to end Miami's drive. Then ND's Jordan Faison returned the ensuing punt 55 yards to the Miami 30. Great start to the second half for the Irish. We're back in action in South Bend as Miami starts with the ball. A Hurricanes team that averages almost 48 points per game has been held to 3 in the fist half. They're struggling to move the ball without star receiver Malachi Toney, who's out with an ankle injury. CJ Carr engineers an impressive 2-minute drive and caps it with an 18-yard strike to Micah Gilbert for the TD. It'll be 3rd and goal from the 1 coming back from a timeout. Jordan Faison makes an excellent back-shoulder catch and taps his toe in bounds for the 27-yard pass from CJ Carr. Notre Dame 10, Miami 0 After the teams traded punts, Notre Dame ripped off a big play to get into Miami territory just before the end of the 1st quarter. ND still leads Miami 3-0. I have a feeling this might be a first to 20 points wins type of game, especially given Malachi Toney's absence. Mark Fletcher is dropped for a 5-yard loss on 3rd down and that ends Miami's drive near midfield. The Irish get points on their opening drive via a 44-yard field goal. entry.title: Chev Clarke beats Chris Billam-Smith at London's Copper Box arena - BBC
entry.body: Billam-Smith stopped as Clarke repeats amateur win - Published Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight on Saturday. Londoner Clarke landed a big right hand at the start of the seventh round and although Billam-Smith beat the count, he was down again moments later after a barrage of punches. The contest was allowed to continue but the Bournemouth fighter looked unsteady on his legs and when Clarke connected with two more blows, the referee stepped in. Billam-Smith immediately protested against the decision, while Clarke stood in the middle of the ring shrugging his shoulders. Clarke moves to 13 wins with two defeats and inflicts the third professional defeat for Billam-Smith who also lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019. "I do what champions do," said Clarke, who also beat Billam-Smith when they met in the amateur ranks a decade ago. Arsenal won and I won. My training camp was good and you saw that in the ring. I'll take all-comers going forward." The likes of heavyweight Johnny Fisher, Traitors star King Kenny and strongman Eddie Hall were all spotted watching on from ringside in a Copper Box arena that was far from full, with just the lower tier of seats open for fans. After a slow start to the contest with lots of holding, Clarke looked the sharper man as he landed some clean shots on the former world champion. In the second round, the Londoner landed a big overhand right to the side of Billam-Smith's head. Clarke also connected in the third round with a big uppercut and an overhand right that snapped back Billam-Smith's head. The former world champion, struggling to find his rhythm, was caught by another uppercut before Billam-Smith responded with a short right hook that made Clarke stumble back to his corner. But in the seventh round Clarke broke Billam-Smith down, scoring two quick knockdowns before the referee intervened. Fight promoter Dana White said after the fight that he felt the decision to stop the fight might have been a little premature. Bentley beats bloodied Mosley Jr and calls out Benn In the main support bout, Britain's Denzel Bentley beat a bloodied and brave Shane Mosley Jr, out-classing the American to win via a unanimous points decision. Bentley scored a big knockdown in the second round, landing a straight right hand that made Mosley stagger backwards before following up with another right hand that dropped him to the canvas. Mosley survived the count and the rest of the round but was routinely tagged by Bentley throughout the contest. The Londonder landed sharp shots off the back foot and in the fifth round drew blood over the right eye of Mosley. Bentley ended the fight strongly, boxing at times with his hands down and moving round his opponent as he landed eye-catching shots that attracted applause from the fans. After 10 rounds the scorecards read 96-94 96-93 95-94 in Bentley's favour, with the 31-year-old then pointing at Conor Benn in the audience and suggesting a potential future match-up between the two. Bentley was stripped of his WBO middleweight title in late October having agreed to fight Mosley instead of face his mandatory challenger. His interim title was previously elevated to a full world championship belt following Janibek Alimkhanuly's decision to move up to super-middleweight. entry.title: Lane Kiffin falls flat against Alabama as massive LSU hype crashes into reality - CBS Sports
entry.body: When Lane Kiffin got off the bus for the Tiger Walk before the Alabama game, he was flanked by Shaquille O'Neal and Angel Reese. Kevin Costner -- Kevin freaking Costner! -- walked behind him and shook his hand. No one has brought more attention and hype to a college football program this year than Kiffin. He signed a seven-year, $91 million contract, tied with two-time national champion Kirby Smart for the second-highest in college football. According to 247Sports, his roster is the most expensive in college football, approaching $50 million. And then, Alabama walked into the building. The Field of Dreams turned into a nightmare. 14 LSU collapsed under the weight of expectation against No. 5 Alabama, losing 31-13 in blowout fashion. After taking a 13-10 lead in the third quarter, the Tigers allowed 21 unanswered points for Kiffin's sixth straight loss against the Crimson Tide. With the loss, LSU sits at 6-3 and 0-3 against teams in the CFP Rankings. Their most impressive performance is arguably a one-point loss to No. 6 Kentucky on the road. While Kiffin has raised LSU's floor, putting unranked teams into the dirt, he has no-showed against real national competition. In every high-leverage moment, Alabama smoked LSU. The Tide held LSU to a field goal after first-and-goal. They forced a missed field goal, then set up a touchdown from great field position. LSU turned it over on downs three times, including twice in the fourth quarter, and turned the ball over twice. And what makes matters worse is that Kiffin's signature offense was completely outdueled by Alabama defensive coordinator Kane Wommack. Statistically, LSU managed to put up 457 yards, but the numbers go deeper. They finished in the 19th percentile for yards per play, 20th percentile for EPA per play and 1st percentile for Explosive Play Rate, according to Game on Paper. Essentially, LSU didn't do anything to truly force Alabama's defense to adjust. That's a hard pill to swallow when you've built your career on being an offensive savant. Kiffin had a great run at Ole Miss, elevating the program to new heights, especially by working with the Grove Collective to improve their NIL operation. With his roster left behind, Pete Golding led Ole Miss to the national semifinals last year. Kiffin has still never actually coached a postseason game, a streak that will likely continue this year. LSU still has two more shots against No. 13 Tennessee for ranked wins, but the Tigers team that shows up against elite teams simply isn't good enough to win both games. If they split the result, LSU would finish 8-4 with a 1-4 record against CFP Top 25 opponents. After the season, most of the best players on the roster will be gone to the NFL. Kiffin will have to start all over again, building through the transfer portal. For the first time since 2016, the top two recruits in Louisiana are heading out of state. Adding insult to injury, No. 3 quarterback Elijah Haven -- a Baton Rouge native -- picked Kalen DeBoer and the Tide over Kiffin. Kiffin walked into Baton Rouge with an unbelievable amount of hype, landing Vanity Fair covers and dominating the interview circuit. When he got the job, Louisiana senator John Kenny joked, all of this nonsense is worth it -- but he better win. And after yet another embarrassing loss to Alabama, he could be heading for a painful offseason.
entry.summary: Lane Kiffin falls flat against Alabama as massive LSU hype crashes into reality CBS Sports LSU flops on fourth downs in 'really disappointing' loss ESPN Alabama finally puts it all together, dominates LSU and leaves Lane Kiffin staring at $40 million CFP disaster Fox News Photos: Bama Tramples LSU 31-13 The Advocate Alabama backs up top-5 CFP ranking as Lane Kiffin’s LSU comes up short again The New York Times

entry.title: Stephen Colbert rushed out of Harvard event, accosted by union protesters - New York Post
entry.body: Stephen Colbert rushed out of Harvard event, accosted by union protesters See more of our coverage in your search results. Liberal former late-night host Stephen Colbert had to be rushed out of an event at Harvard after someone pulled a fire alarm as hundreds of union protesters shouted outside over his decision to cross their picket line and give a talk at the school, according to reports. Cellist Yo-Yo Ma took the stage with Colbert Thursday despite pleas from the Harvard Graduate Student Union urging them to cancel in solidarity. Despite the protests, the union members denied responsibility for pulling the alarm. “The alarm was unrelated to HGSU’s picketing activity and we have no knowledge of its cause,” wrote HGSU in a statement on social media. “Members at the picket were relieved to learn that no one inside was at risk,” the statement continued. The union was hoping that Colbert — who stood with protesters during the Writers Guild strike in 2023 and co-founded Strike Force Five — and Yo Yo Ma, a Harvard graduate, would avoid walking the picket line. Even before the alarm, the celebrity appearance was disrupted by the union members chanting and demonstrating directly outside the venue, making it difficult to hear the speakers. The fire alarm forced organizers to pull the plug during the question and answer portion of the talk and escort Colbert out of the venue. HGSU has been on strike since Oct. 27, demanding a fair contract that includes wage increases and protections for non-citizens and harassment and discrimination. Since the strike began, graduate classes have been untaught. The union said Colbert got plenty of warning that they would consider his appearnce to be crossing their picket lines. “HGSU-UAW sent multiple formal communications to Colbert and Ma’s teams well in advance of the event that due to ongoing strike action, the building their event would be held at would be one with an active picket and that we encouraged them to move their event to an off-site location or virtually, reschedule the event, or cancel so as to not cross the picket,” wrote the union on Instagram. “Colbert and Ma’s respective unions, SAG-AFTRA and the Boston Musicians’ Association, also reached out to them on our behalf with the same request,” the statement continued. “They continued the event inside without regard for the picket line, and refused to speak with union members as they left the event. In other words — they crossed our picket line.” John Green, an American author and YouTuber, stood in solidarity with HGSU and changed his schedule to accommodate the strike. “They’re on strike and I had to move a thing to not cross a picket line,” he said in an interview clip posted to HGSU’s Instagram. “Which was an easy decision… it was not a hard decision for me. I’m sorry I had to do it on Zoom,” he continued. “But I’m also sorry that the student workers have to be on strike against the richest university in the world.” He donated the proceeds he earned from the event to the union, according to The Boston Globe. The Harvard Graduate Student Union and representatives for Yo Yo Ma and Stephen Colbert did not immediately respond to The Post’s request for comment.
entry.summary: Stephen Colbert rushed out of Harvard event, accosted by union protesters New York Post Yo-Yo Ma, Stephen Colbert canceled by striking Harvard union Cambridge Day Stephen Colbert, Yo-Yo Ma event at Harvard cut short by fire alarm as demonstrators chant outside The Boston Globe Yo-Yo Ma is silenced at Harvard Slipped Disc Stephen Colbert's talk at Harvard abruptly ends amid striking union students AOL.com

entry.title: 'Heated Rivalry' Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie (Exclusive) - Deadline
entry.body: EXCLUSIVE: Heated Rivalry fans who have been eagerly awaiting Season 2 of Crave‘s hockey series are in for a great surprise. The hugely popular romantic drama starring Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams has not one but two six-episode seasons on the way, sources tell Deadline. And that’s not all, there is a movie coming up, too. The two seasons are currently filming back-to-back, sources said. As they wrap at the end of November or beginning of December, a standalone Heated Rivalry film will shoot in December, I hear. Described as a Christmas special or a holiday-themed episode, it is planned for a theatrical release next December, I’m told. According to sources, Storrie’s Ilya and Williams’ Shane are not in it. Details are murky but I hear it is centered on the other Season 1 couple, Scott (François Arnaud) and Kip (Robbie G.K.), with additional characters from the series also featured. It’s worth noting that Rachel Reid, the author of the bestselling Game Changers book series that Heated Rivalry is based on, has written a short story, Merry Christmas, Scott and Kip!, which depicts the duo’s first Christmas together. Watch on Deadline A rep for Canadian streamer Crave said that there are no projects to confirm. Speculation that Heated Rivalry may be filming two seasons back-to-back has percolated for a while, fueled by a leaked August Cameo video by recurring guest star Dylan Walsh in which he said “I think we’re doing 12 [episodes] this time” before briefly writing in his profile that “a video went viral that got me in trouble.” Some interpreted his comments as Season 2 being supersized. Heated Rivalry creator Jacob Tierney last month debunked that theory, confirming to Andy Cohen that like Season 1, Season 2 will consist of 6 episodes. Neither he nor Crave have acknowledged a Season 3 pickup but Tierney said in the same SiriusXM interview with Cohen that they will be done filming by the end of the year without specifying what exactly the shoot covers. As for theatrical distribution, Heated Rivalry, which streams on HBO Max in the U.S. and several other key territories, has dabbled in that. The series’ six-episode first season is currently available for a limited run at Regal Cinema, AMC and Cinemark locations for paired-episode screenings. As of Saturday morning, 880 theaters reported collecting $420K on Friday in what looks to be a strong $1.3M opening weekend. Season 2 of Heated Rivalry is confirmed to premiere in spring 2027, with April launch likely. It’s been almost a year since the ice hockey romance premiered on Nov. 28, taking pop culture by storm and turning actors Storrie and Williams from complete unknowns to global superstars overnight. After Season 1 adapted Book 2, Heated Rivalry, which chronicles the budding romance between rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie), while also incorporating elements from Book 1, Game Changer (featuring Scott and Kip), Season 2 is expected to continue Shane and Ilya’s story by tackling Book 6, The Long Game, while also introducing a new couple from Role Model, Harris Drover and Troy Barrett, played by Justice Smith and Charlie Gillespie, respectively and possibly incorporating elements from other tomes in the series. Emily Hampshire, Brendan Morgan, David Tomlinson and Lauren Chan are among the new cast additions announced for Season 2. An interesting stunt here for Crave’s Heated Rivalry: Regal via their Regal Entertainment Distribution is releasing paired season one episodes of the hit Bell/HBO series this weekend.

entry.title: ‘Club Kid’ Scene-Stealer Kirby Howell-Baptiste on Playing a Drugged-Up Party Girl Who Turns Jordan Firstman’s World Upside Down: She’s ‘A Complete Tornado’
entry.body: “Last week she goes and tops herself — she fucking killed herself, babe.” In the midst of making these life-changing and upsetting revelations in the most wonderfully insensitive manner possible, Edison inquires if Peter and her should “do a bump” of coke (slightly shaken by how his life is quickly unravelling, he declines). “[Edison] is just a complete tornado,” says Londoner Howell-Baptiste, adding that she thinks the character is an “amalgamation of a few party people” Firstman has encountered. “But what I really love is that, although she’s absolutely bananas, she does feel quite real and quite relatable. I think everyone knows that person, to some degree. At some point in your life, you have met that person.” Edison isn’t seen again in “Club Kid” after the apartment scene, in which she eventually leaves Arlo in Peter’s care and — predictably — fails to return to collect him as promised later on. But as Peter begins a frantic search to find her across various New York house parties, further levels of her comically debauched behaviour come to light, as he hears how she was kicked out of several places for simply being too much of a tornado to handle.
entry.summary: “Should we do a bump?” It’s a line said, in various forms, numerous times across the first half of “Club Kid,” Jordan Firstman’s hedonistic and heartfelt coming-of-age comedy drama about a hard-partying New York club promoter suddenly forced to grapple with life and responsibilities. entry.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
entry.body: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack - Published At least six people were killed and more than a dozen others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Three bodies were found at his home when it was searched by police. Here is everything we know so far. How did the attack unfold? The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city which is popular with tourists. Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car". Footage shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard. A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. A 25-year-old man who was arrested remains in hospital after having surgery for a gunshot wound. The Krakow branch of the National Public Prosecutor's Office in Poland has announced an investigation into what constitutes "a terrorist offence". Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times. The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself. Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor. City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues. The suspect's car, found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, was checked for possible explosive devices, police said, but none were found. Residents of nearby buildings had been evacuated while the operation was under way. How many people have died and been injured? Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in central Krakow, including a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack. On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and his sister, who was 21-years-old. Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia. Tusk later named the injured officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur MoraÅski. One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added. In an update on Sunday, police spokesperson Katarzyna Cislo told Radio Krakow two women who were sent to hospital following the incident had been released and the remaining individuals in Krakow's hospitals are in a stable condition. She said this included the two police officers who were injured. Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims. What do we know about the suspect and motive? Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name. Local governor Krzysztof Jan KlÄczar said the gunman remains in a critical condition at hospital. The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities said he was not a soldier. "Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added. Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details. His home in Ostrowiec ÅwiÄtokrzyski, a city around 200km (125 miles) from Krakow, has been searched with support from counter-terrorism police. How did witnesses describe the attack? The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination. Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started. Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down. "A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises." Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend. She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice". Local media outlet Gazeta Krakowska reported two surgeons rushed to help after the shooting stopped. Dr Mateusz Wierdak and Prof MichaÅ PÄdziwiatr spoke to the media outlet saying they helped the wounded after having lunch with their families. PÄdziwiatr says two police officers "were conscious, in superficial contact with gunshot wounds to the chest", adding: "The perpetrator was also conscious, expressed pain, and had gunshot wounds to the abdomen, thigh, and chest." "We don't feel like heroes, but we did everything a paramedic would do at the scene of such an incident." What has the reaction been in Poland and internationally? After travelling to Krakow, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said : "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism...that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow." Krakow Mayor Åukasz GibaÅa has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, 11 November. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I'm shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in KrakÃ³w today." "My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added. British foreign secretary Ed Miliband said on social media the UK government "deeply mourns" those who died in the "appalling attack". US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack". The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland". President Volodymyr Zelensky of neighbouring Ukraine called the shooting "shocking." "On behalf of the Ukrainian people, and personally, I extend my sincere condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims," he wrote on social media. Additional reporting by Olivia Ireland
entry.summary: Six people were killed in a random shooting in Krakow's main square, and three bodies were later found at the home of the attacker.

entry.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russia ramping up attacks to ‘pressure’ Kyiv at trilateral talks, Zelenskyy says - The Guardian
entry.body: - Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of intensifying strikes across the country to put pressure on Kyiv at upcoming talks after an overnight barrage triggered power cuts as temperatures drop. “By intensifying its attacks on Ukraine and our infrastructure at this very moment, Russia is trying to additionally lay the groundwork for putting pressure on Ukraine’s position and that of its partners,” the Ukrainian president said. “Russia perceives diplomacy in its own peculiar way – as a form of aggression.” - Ukraine’s energy ministry said “a massive attack on a number of energy facilities” on Saturday had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding regions. Russia had throughout the night launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, Zelenskyy said, among which were KN-23 missiles manufactured and supplied by North Korea. - The strikes came before a US-brokered trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi scheduled for next week aimed at reviving stalled diplomatic efforts towards peace. Ukrainian officials are expected to sit down with Russian negotiators and US envoys on Tuesday and Wednesday for the first such talks in months. The diplomatic track has been stalled since February when Washington shifted attention to its war with Iran. - Zelenskyy also urged the US to increase its flagging aid to Ukraine. “Unfortunately, there is still a significant shortage of interceptors for Patriot systems, and the United States is in the best position to help address it,” he said. - Italy’s foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, on Saturday said he had been targeted by pro-Russian hackers over his backing for Ukraine. Tajani said in a post on X that “backing in a transparent way the freedom and independence of a sovereign state” had made him a target. Tajani said his personal data had been published on the dark web and that the hackers were seeking further information about him and his family and were willing to pay for it. - The Italian prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, who has been one of the strongest backers of Ukraine among western leaders, expressed her support for Tajani and said the sale of confidential information relating to public officials was “a matter of serious concern”. Moscow has not commented on the incident. - France’s far-left presidential contender Jean-Luc Mélenchon said on Saturday that settling the Ukraine conflict could not be done by granting territorial concessions without consulting the people concerned. Melenchon, who polls suggest could reach the second round of next year’s presidential election, set out his France Unbowed party’s foreign policy positions at a rally just outside Paris. - Mélenchon has been criticised in the past for questioning the legitimacy of Zelenskyy. But in a campaign speech to thousands of supporters, he said an administration run by his party would take an active role in settling the war in Ukraine. Europe would have to play an active role in peace talks, he said. “We cannot accept that one could consider a peace with territorial concessions in Ukraine without asking the populations concerned if they agree or not to be on one side or other of the border,” he said. “It is for the people themselves to decide what they want,” he added. - A Ukrainian attack killed one person in Russia’s Belgorod region when a drone hit a private home in the town of Grayvoron, local officials said on Saturday. Russia’s defence ministry said its forces shot down 411 Ukrainian drones overnight over 10 Russian regions, including Belgorod. Drones were also destroyed over the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black and Azov seas, it said. Russian media outlets later reported that the Saratov Oil Refinery had been hit and shared images of plumes of smoke over the city.
entry.summary: Ukraine war briefing: Russia ramping up attacks to ‘pressure’ Kyiv at trilateral talks, Zelenskyy says The Guardian Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity Al Jazeera Hundreds of thousands left without power in Ukraine after Russian strikes, authorities say CBS News Russia pounds power facilities around Kyiv, damages major bridge Reuters Ukraine's power network suffers further damage after fresh Russian strikes BBC

entry.title: Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh damaged after attempted attack - CNBC
entry.body: An administrative building belonging to state oil giant Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was damaged by falling debris following an attempted attack on Sunday, with no injuries or fatalities reported, the kingdom's Energy Ministry said. A Reuters witness saw blown-out windows across several floors of the Aramco Tower, one of the tallest buildings in the capital's King Abdullah Financial District. The incident, which the ministry said caused limited damage, came after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted two missiles fired by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis towards Riyadh. Aramco was not immediately available for comment, and there was no immediate statement from the Houthis. Multiple loud booms were heard in Riyadh earlier on Sunday, a Reuters witness said, shortly after Saudi Civil Defense issued an early-warning alert of a potential threat in the region. Authorities later announced that the danger had passed. The Saudi-led coalition that has been fighting the Houthis subsequently said it had intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles in Riyadh and the kingdom's southern region. The Houthis have stepped up missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities since fighting resumed in July and became another front in the wider Middle East war reignited following the US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February. Saudi Arabia has carried out airstrikes against Houthi targets in Yemen. Alerts in oil-rich eastern province Earlier on Sunday, Saudi Civil Defense issued and later lifted warnings in several areas of the oil-rich Eastern Province, including Dhahran, home to the headquarters of state oil giant Saudi Aramco. The Eastern Province holds most of the kingdom's oil and gas reserves. Saudi Aramco's headquarters suffered extensive damage in an attack in October. An attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Oct. 10 killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, according to Saudi authorities. The renewed hostilities have shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce that had largely halted fighting between the two sides. Saudi Arabia led a coalition of Arab states into Yemen in 2015 to restore the internationally recognised government after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa. The latest escalation comes a day after Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry said Saudi airstrikes killed at least 33 people near Sanaa. Saudi authorities said they were investigating.

entry.title: Putin Seizes Three More Japan Tobacco Businesses, Bringing Takeover to $3.7 Billion - UNITED24 Media
entry.body: - Category - War in Ukraine Putin Seizes Three More Japan Tobacco Businesses, Bringing Takeover to $3.7 Billion Russian leader Vladimir Putin has placed three additional subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco International (JTI) under Russian-appointed management, expanding Moscow’s takeover of the Japanese tobacco giant’s operations to seven companies, with the affected assets valued at up to $3.7 billion. We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field. According to The Moscow Times on November 7, the latest presidential decree transferred control of JTI Russia, Pereslavl-Tabak, and JTI Innovative Products to the Russian company Industrial Assets. The decision follows a separate decree issued on November 5 that placed four JTI manufacturing and tobacco-related businesses under the same management structure. Bloomberg reported that the newly affected companies include a holding entity, a cigarette distribution business, and an importer of electronic tobacco products and heated tobacco systems. The earlier takeover covered Petro, JTI Donskoy Tabak, Kres Neva, and JTI Yelets, which collectively employ approximately 4,000 people. According to The Moscow Times, Russian industry analysts estimate the combined value of the affected assets at 250 billion to 300 billion rubles, or approximately $3.1 billion to $3.7 billion. Industrial Assets was established in September 2026. Russian corporate records identify Sergei Dremov, a former member of the State Council of Russian-occupied Crimea, as one of its founders. His biography indicates that he served in Russian state security agencies between 2000 and 2016. JTI has operated in Russia since 1999 and previously controlled up to 40% of the country’s cigarette market, selling brands including Winston, Camel, Sobranie, and LD. entry.title: Drone attack on Colombian army base kills three soldiers and wounds 16 - Al Jazeera
entry.body: Drone attack on Colombian army base kills three soldiers and wounds 16 Colombian President de la Espriella says those behind the attack in Santa Rosa del Sur will have ‘nowhere to hide’. A drone attack on a military base in northern Colombia has killed three soldiers and wounded at least 16, the country’s armed forces said. The Colombian military said in a statement on Saturday that the attack hit a base in Santa Rosa del Sur, a small town in the foothills of the San Lucas mountain range. Authorities have not said who carried out the strike, the latest in a series of attacks on security forces as violence rises across rural parts of the country. The area is rich in gold mines and has long been disputed by rebel armed groups including the Gulf Clan, the National Liberation Army (ELN) and smaller groups led by former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC). Footage shared on social media showed clouds of smoke rising from the base after three explosions, and soldiers taking cover in shelters made of sandbags. “Those who were behind this attack… will have nowhere to hide,” President Abelardo de la Espriella wrote on X. “Every attack against our soldiers strengthens our resolve to defend Colombia.” Rising violence Violence has intensified in several rural areas since de la Espriella, a conservative, took office in August. The president cancelled peace talks with rebel groups and has taken a confrontational approach, including more air strikes, deploying more troops in some cities and creating joint task forces to defend strategic assets such as a pipeline that runs from the Caribbean coast to central Colombia. De la Espriella’s government argues that armed groups used ceasefires granted by the previous government to consolidate their grip on rural areas, where they tax local businesses and profit from the drug trade. Some groups have responded by stepping up attacks on the country’s armed forces. Last week, a military base in Tolima province was targeted with missiles made from gas canisters. The attack killed four civilians, including a two-month-old baby. Police in the border city of Cucuta have been attacked several times with remotely activated bombs. State forces and illegal armed groups carried out 34 attacks with bombs or explosives in Colombia in the four weeks to October 16, a 9 percent increase on last year’s four-week average, according to ACLED, a group that monitors armed conflicts. A 2016 peace deal with FARC led to the demobilisation of more than 14,000 fighters, but smaller groups have since fought over the rebels’ former territory.

entry.title: Mapping how France’s protest wave spread across Europe - Al Jazeera
entry.body: Mapping how France’s protest wave spread across Europe More than 1,700 cost-of-living demonstrations have taken place in 31 European countries since mid-September, with France leading the way. France’s protest movement is showing little sign of easing, nearly two months after high school students first walked out over crumbling classrooms. On Saturday, 146,000 people rallied across the country, including 46,000 in Paris, according to the Ministry of the Interior, while unions put the figures at 250,000 and 75,000. Turnout was down from previous weeks, but police used tear gas and batons on protesters in Paris and fired tear gas canisters at hundreds of people blocking a road in central Lyon, France’s third-largest city. About 70,000 security personnel were deployed, days after an estimated 575,000 people joined a union-organised rally. The protests have expanded to cover a range of issues, from high fuel prices to wages and social housing, and in some cases, the demonstrations have been marred by looting and violence. Police have been accused of using excessive force, with officers using barricades, tear gas and batons against protesters. Al Jazeera maps where demonstrations, including riots, have taken place across Europe. Demonstrations began in France An analysis of data from Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) found that between September 15 and October 30, more than 1,200 protests and riots of 100 or more people took place across France over education, public services and the cost of living. The movement began in mid-September in high schools, where students complained of overcrowded classrooms, a lack of teachers and crumbling buildings. It soon broadened into protests against the rising cost of living, drawing in trade unions and the “yellow vests” movement, with rioting and looting on the sidelines. On October 17 alone, more than 500,000 people protested nationwide, according to government estimates. ACLED CEO Clionadh Raleigh said on October 19 that ACLED had recorded an average of 20.5 demonstrations a day in France over the past five years. “During the current protest cycle, that has jumped to almost 66 a day, more than three times the usual rate,” she said. Protest cycles typically last about 20 days, or 36 for major movements, Raleigh said. By ACLED’s count, this one had reached 45 days and was still going. “But the most striking difference is the level of confrontation,” she said. “Almost a quarter of events, 24.2 percent, have been classified as riots, compared to a median of just 1.9 percent in previous cycles. Only the unrest following the death of Nahel Merzouk in 2023 recorded a higher proportion.” The police response has also drawn criticism. On October 28, four United Nations experts mandated by the Human Rights Council expressed alarm at the “excessive use of force” by French authorities in dispersing the student protests. “The scale of the arrests and detention, affecting several thousand people, mainly minors, appears disproportionate and deters demonstrators from exercising their freedoms of expression and peaceful assembly,” they said in a statement. In the northern city of Lille, a teenager lost a hand when a grenade exploded as school protesters clashed with police. Protests across Europe France is not protesting alone. Since mid-September, demonstrations over rising living costs, low wages and a lack of public services have broken out in 30 other European countries, from Portugal to Poland. Between September 15 and October 30, more than 1,700 protests and riots of 100 or more people took place across Europe, according to an analysis of ACLED data. Although protests in other countries did not reach the same scale as the rallies in France, they may be a sign of discontent spilling over, Alberto Alemanno, professor of European Union law and policy at HEC Paris Business School, told Al Jazeera last month. “France is the epicentre of this movement … and there are signs now that this is spreading beyond France,” Alemanno said. Which country has had the most protests? France has led the demonstrations, but protests have also broken out across Europe at the same time, driven by a common thread of underfunded education, rising living costs and unaffordable housing. According to an analysis of ACLED data, France saw more than 1,200 protests and riots between September 15 and October 30, followed by Spain (173), Italy (160), Germany (70) and Portugal (33). In Spain, tens of thousands of people rallied in early October after parliament rejected two emergency housing decrees on October 2, dealing a blow to Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s minority government. In Italy, demonstrations over the cost-of-living crisis and unaffordable housing have led to clashes with police. In Portugal, tens of thousands of protesters marched against the cost-of-living crisis, low wages and an inability to access housing in major cities.
entry.summary: Mapping how France’s protest wave spread across Europe Al Jazeera In pictures: France protests draw 146,000 as clashes erupt for fourth straight weekend CNBC Paris agitators defy police orders, renew nationwide protests centered in Paris Fox News France sees new round of student and Yellow Vest protests in Paris and dozens of cities DW.com Another Day of France’s Protests Unfurl During an Autumn of Discontent The New York Times

entry.title: Want to fly to the moon? NASA is looking for new astronauts to help grow its Artemis program - NBC News
entry.body: — Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base? NASA is accepting applications for a new astronaut class that will help grow the Artemis program. Officials announced the news Saturday during a Kennedy Space Center air show promoting lunar exploration as well as advances in aviation and technology. NASA’s last call for new astronauts was two years ago. More than 8,000 applied, with 10 making the final cut in September 2025. With only 32 active astronauts, the space agency needs more recruits as it looks to expand humanity’s presence beyond low-Earth orbit as quickly as possible. April’s lunar flyaround by the Artemis II crew kicked off the lunar campaign. “We have far more work than we have astronauts,” Artemis III commander Randy Bresnik told The Associated Press on Saturday. Aspiring astronauts have between now and Dec. 3 to submit their applications. NASA expects to make its final selection by late 2027, with the new candidates beginning their training by early 2028 — the same year that NASA intends to return astronauts to the lunar surface after an absence of more than half a century. Bresnik and his three crewmates will blast into orbit next summer to practice docking their capsule with a pair of lunar landers, one built by Elon Musk’s SpaceX and the other by Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin. Their mission will stick close to Earth — no lunar flyby — and serve as a dress rehearsal for the following year’s Artemis IV mission that will attempt to land two astronauts near the lunar south pole. The moon base will materialize as more rovers, robots, structures and power grids are launched. Patience is essential for becoming an astronaut, noted Artemis III’s Frank Rubio, whose 371 consecutive days in space is a U.S. Candidates must also be U.S. citizens with college degrees and professional work experience. The two years of mandatory training can be grueling, and it could take another several years on top of that before finally rocketing into space. “It’s important for them to realize most of that work is not going to the moon, right?” Rubio told the AP. “That will be about 1% of your experience. What you’re doing is contributing to the mission of going to the moon.” This will be NASA’s 25th astronaut class since the original Mercury Seven in 1959.

entry.title: Artemis II Rocket Was Powerful Enough To Disrupt GPS - Hackaday
entry.body: Rockets certainly have a substantial impact if you ever see a launch in person. The noise, shock waves, and even heat can be awe-inspiring. What is less obvious are the impacts a launch has on our upper atmosphere, or “anthropogenic space weather” as the fancy scientists call it. A pre-print from a recent study on Artemis II’s impact on our atmosphere shows a shockingly wide range of effects. As a whole, the impact on Artemis comes in waves. Each stage of the Space Launch System performs burns in different parts of the atmosphere, creating increasing ripples as the rocket moves through various layers. The first stage is the largest in terms of thrust, but has limited impact on the ionosphere because of how low it occurred. The 2nd and 3rd stages’ impact, however, was so large that it could’ve sustainably disrupted GPS signals at the time. Waves even traveled through the atmosphere across the entirety of North America in the form of gravity waves. These ionosphere “holes” might not be a major problem now, but it’s something to think about as we ramp up rocket production. While this research relied on thousands of sensors across the globe, that doesn’t mean you need the same budget to analyze the state of the ionosphere at home.
entry.summary: Artemis II Rocket Was Powerful Enough To Disrupt GPS Hackaday Artemis II launch tore a hole in Earth's atmosphere, say scientists BBC Sky at Night Magazine NASA rocket may have punched a hole in the atmosphere, here's how it could impact GPS signals WUSA9 NASA's Artemis II moon launch tore a hole in Earth's upper atmosphere so huge it disrupted GPS signals Space Artemis II moon launch was so powerful it punched a hole in atmosphere USA Today

entry.title: Two paths, one flux: Trapped ions simulate Aharonov–Bohm interference in a lattice gauge theory - Phys.org
entry.body: November 7, 2026 feature Two paths, one flux: Trapped ions simulate Aharonov–Bohm interference in a lattice gauge theory Tejasri Gururaj Author Gaby Clark Scientific Editor Robert Egan Senior Editor In a new Nature Physics study, researchers demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a quantum simulation of a lattice gauge theory using a hybrid trapped-ion quantum computer. Gauge theories describe how matter interacts through fields called gauge fields, which carry the electromagnetic, weak and strong forces. They form the basis of the Standard Model of particle physics. In lattice gauge theories, space is modeled as a grid with matter at the vertices and gauge fields on the links connecting them. Quantum simulators offer a way to study these theories. However, most quantum simulations of the simplest version—the Z₂ lattice gauge theory—have been limited to one spatial dimension, where effects linked to magnetic flux cannot appear. To address this issue, researchers from the University of Oxford have now used trapped ions to simulate a Z₂ lattice gauge theory in a quasi-two-dimensional loop. The trapped ions perform a dual role. Their electronic states encode the gauge fields and their vibrations encode the matter. Phys.org spoke to the first author of the study, Sebastian Saner, about the work. "We first started brainstorming how to use a hybrid trapped-ion quantum system to simulate lattice gauge theories back in 2022. Later, during the project, we had the idea of using entangled qubits to encode the gauge-field flux. Coming up with this idea was one of the particularly exciting moments for us during the project," said Saner. Using two trapped ions, the team built a closed loop to see how a flux stored in entangled qubits would affect a moving particle. Matter, fields and flux "Gauge theories describe how particles interact with each other through gauge fields. A simple example is two electrons repelling each other through the electromagnetic field," explained Saner. "In this picture, the electrons are described by a matter field, while the electromagnetic field is the gauge field that mediates their interaction." Some of the most puzzling materials in physics, such as quantum spin liquids and high-temperature superconductors, are also described by gauge theories. Here, the gauge fields emerge from the collective behavior of electrons. Physicists often describe these materials using Z₂ lattice gauge theories, the simplest type, in which the field at each link of a grid can take only two values. In these theories, the two values represent whether a field line is present or absent. Z₂ lattice gauge theories are also relevant to topological quantum error correction. Simulating these theories on classical computers is challenging. According to Saner, computational complexity generally grows exponentially with system size, particularly in higher dimensions. The physics also becomes richer with each additional dimension. For instance, in two spatial dimensions, links can form closed loops, which can be pierced by a magnetic flux. This gives rise to quasiparticles called visons, which have no counterpart in one dimension, where no loops can form. Earlier experiments have studied Z₂ lattice gauge theories using cold atoms and superconducting qubits, but mostly in one-dimensional setups. Some experiments have simulated two-dimensional geometries, but removed the matter fields to simplify the model. As a result, these approaches could not capture how moving charges and gauge fields influence each other, including how flux affects particle motion. Ions doing double duty "Trapped ions naturally have both qubits and vibrational modes. Typically, the ions' vibrations are cooled close to their ground state and used to mediate interactions between qubits, but are not directly used to store quantum information," explained Saner. Two electronic energy levels of a strontium ion served as a qubit, representing the gauge field on a link. The ion's vibrations, behaving like harmonic oscillators, served as the matter sites. An oscillator can hold any number of units of vibrational energy, or phonons. In this simulation, a single phonon represents a matter particle. "The advantage is that matter fields can be stored much more efficiently in the vibrational modes," said Saner. The geometry of the lattice is determined by which qubits and vibrational modes are coupled together, not by the ions' physical positions. Even with the ions in a single line, these connections can create loops and other geometries that the arrangement alone can't. Dimensions created this way are known as synthetic dimensions. To make the phonon hop, the researchers used a laser to apply two forces, each acting on a different vibrational mode and each pushing in a direction set by the qubit's state. In simple terms, each time the particle hops between sites, the field line on the link switches between present and absent. This ties the particle's motion to the gauge field, as the theory requires. The team first used a single ion to simulate one link connecting two matter sites. Adding a second ion introduced a second qubit, and so a second link between the same two sites. The result was a loop, which gave the particle two paths to choose from. To encode the flux through this loop, the researchers entangled the two link qubits. One entangled state corresponded to zero flux, while the other corresponded to a nonzero flux, representing a vison. "The hardest part was combining all the different ingredients and translating the theoretical ideas into a feasible experiment," Saner noted. "This involved getting the hybrid interactions to the required level of control, as well as developing the necessary state preparation and readout techniques." Frozen by flux With a single ion, the researchers observed the particle tunnel back and forth between the two sites, with the field line switching between present and absent. This is consistent with the Z₂ version of Gauss's law. As the particle moved away from the starting site, a field line stretched out behind it and disappeared when the particle returned to the site. In these first runs, the researchers set the energy cost of creating a field line to zero. When the team then added the cost, the oscillations became faster but smaller, and the particle no longer moved fully from one site to the other. Because every move required creating a field line, moving became energetically costly. According to the researchers, this tunneling suppression is a precursor to confinement in larger systems, the effect that binds quarks together inside hadrons. The researchers then moved to the two-ion setup to study the Aharonov–Bohm effect. "The Aharonov–Bohm effect is a phenomenon where, in its original conception, an electron travels along two different paths around a region containing magnetic flux. Even though the magnetic field is zero along the paths of the electron, the interference pattern shifts depending on the magnetic flux," explained Saner. In the loop, the two links play the role of the two paths. As the particle crosses a link, it picks up a phase set by that link's gauge field. In the Z₂ case, this phase is either a plus or minus sign. The flux through the loop determines whether the two paths give the particle the same sign or opposite signs. When the two qubits were entangled in the zero-flux state, both paths gave the particle the same sign, so they added up. The particle tunneled freely between the sites, twice as fast as on a single link. When the two qubits were entangled in the state representing a vison, the two paths gave the particle opposite signs and canceled out. The particle stayed where it started, with its tunneling completely suppressed. The researchers also confirmed that the flux remained constant throughout, except for a slow decay caused by decoherence. Numerical simulations that included known sources of noise, such as heating of the vibrational modes, agreed with the experimental data. Next steps According to the researchers, the results show that the hybrid approach can capture how flux affects the motion of matter, something earlier simulations without matter fields could not. Saner sees two main directions for future work. The first is simulating larger lattices. "Currently, we are simulating a single loop, which in lattice terms is still a very small system and can easily be solved using classical computers. However, even a relatively modest increase in lattice size could make the problem very difficult, if not impossible in practice, to solve using classical computers," said Saner. The second is extending the approach beyond Z₂. "Future work could extend this to Zₙ gauge theories, where the gauge field can take a larger number of values, or even toward the limit N → ∞," Saner explained. Written for you by our author Tejasri Gururaj, edited by Gaby Clark, and fact-checked and reviewed by Robert Egan—this article is the result of careful human work.
