entry.title: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes - BBC
entry.body: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes The Aramco Tower, a skyscraper in the Saudi Arabian capital's central financial district, had been hit by an air attack. A statement issued via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed the group had targeted Riyadh's business zone on Saturday, without mentioning the Aramco Tower by name. The Saudi energy ministry said the tower had suffered only "minor damage" and no one had been killed or injured. Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the building, with at least one floor appearing to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike. Windows on more than one level appear to have been shattered by the strike. The Houthis also said Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities were targeted in separate strikes. Saudi Arabia said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed several missiles. The strikes were the latest claimed by the Yemen-based armed group against targets deep inside Saudi Arabia, which the Gulf power has struggled to contain in recent months. It came a day after the Houthis accused a Saudi-led coalition of killing at least 33 people, including women and children, in an air strike on Yemen. Footage broadcast by Houthi-run television channel Al Masirah showed rescuers pulling bodies from the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa. Saba said 39 people had been injured in the strike. Saudi Arabia has not commented. A Saudi-led coalition has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government, which has lost control of a large swathe of the country to the rebel group. Although the conflict had largely been dormant in recent years, fighting has intensified following the outbreak of the Iran war. An informal ceasefire unravelled in July after the Tehran-backed Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport Saudi Arabia said had been to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing there. Major fighting has since resumed between Houthi forces and troops aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government. The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.
entry.summary: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes BBC Iconic Saudi Tower Hit as Yemen’s Houthis Target Riyadh WSJ Saudi Aramco Tower Damaged as Yemen’s Houthis Attack Riyadh The New York Times Aramco: Building owned by Saudi oil giant damaged in missile attack on Riyadh’s financial district CNN Africa’s most powerful military joins Bahrain, Kuwait and Syria in fierce backlash over Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s $1.7 trillion oil giant, Aramco Business Insider Africa

entry.title: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war - Al Jazeera
entry.body: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war US President Donald Trump warns that United States forces are ‘locked and loaded’ and ready to strike if necessary. Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has warned that Tehran will “rain down hell” if the United States resumes attacks, serving Washington with an ultimatum in an attempt to end the two countries’ eight-month war. “Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results,” Araghchi wrote in a post on X on Sunday. “Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened warriors rain down hell,” he said. US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that renewed strikes on Iran are “highly unlikely” if negotiations progress over Tehran’s nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. ‘Locked and loaded’ “It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump said when asked about continued US strikes on Iran during a phone interview reported by CNN. “I would [continue], if necessary, but we hit them really hard,” he added. Trump warned that US forces have three aircraft carriers stationed in the region “fully locked and loaded”, ready to continue strikes if need be. He also said that the US has 38 bridges in Iran’s crosshairs that US forces “can knock down in literally one hour”. Iran’s Foreign Ministry also quoted Araghchi in an earlier statement on Sunday that said Iran would “not go easy on American targets” in the region. Araghchi’s statements came after reports by state media that an oil tanker caught fire earlier that morning after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, citing Iran’s navy. The navy claimed the ship’s identification systems were turned off and it was travelling in the no-go zone of the strait. ‘Devastating and severe’ response An adviser to Iran’s commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Aerospace Force made threats that echoed those of the Iranian foreign minister and said that weapons have been “secured for years to come”. “The armed forces are at the ready, and if the enemy makes a mistake, Iran’s response will be devastating and severe,” warned IRGC Brigadier-General Ali Belali in a statement on Telegram. “As senior commanders of the armed forces have pointed out, we have upgraded our capabilities in the post-Ramadan War period,” Belali said. The back-and-fourth between Iranian and US leaders comes following US midterm elections in which the Democratic Party won control of both chambers of Congress, soundly defeating Trump’s Republican Party. Araghchi alleged that negotiations have been delayed as a result of the elections, but he awaits the path forward, Iranian state media reported. “It will take some time for things to settle down and for the atmosphere to become conducive to the mediators resuming their visits,” the foreign minister said.
entry.summary: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war Al Jazeera Iran says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on missile ranges, and other Mideast news AP News Iran says missiles no longer bound by range limits Iran International Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest BBC Restrictions on Range of Iranian Missiles Lifted: IRGC Spokesman تسنیم

entry.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
entry.body: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt - Published At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured. The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment. Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched. Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he had ordered state authorities to "investigate the circumstances of the accident, and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent". The public prosecutor's office warned the death toll could rise. The government said hospitals in the area had been put "on heightened alert" as they dealt with a massive influx of patients. Egypt's health minister Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said people were being treated for broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent said it was providing aid and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The driver of one of the trains was among those who died in the crash, the ministry confirmed. The first train involved in the crash was travelling from Giza to Fayoum, south of Cairo, when it crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Images from the scene showed some carriages had overturned, with the body of at least one appearing to have split in two. Trains between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were dispatched to remove the wrecked trains. The railway authority has not said how long it expects this to take. The collision occurred in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat, close to where Egypt's deadliest train tragedy occurred in February 2002, when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor. In that incident, more than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher. Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more. There were calls in Egypt on Sunday for the transport minister to resign over the latest deadly rail disaster. Foreign leaders and dignitaries have shared condolences and support for the victims. Saudi Arabia's ministry of foreign affairs expressed "solidarity" with Egypt and wished those hurt a speedy recovery. Turkey's ambassador to Egypt wrote on X that he extended "heartfelt condolences and sincere sympathy" to the victims, their families, and the Egyptian people.
entry.summary: Several carriages derailed after two trains travelling in the same direction crashed outside the city of Giza.

entry.title: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
entry.body: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says - Published One of two surgeons who treated victims on the streets in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland said his colleague"undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer. The pair were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15. The doctors raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator. On Sunday, the officers - both hailed as "true heroes" by the prime minister for preventing further deaths - emerged from comas. Prosecutors launched a terror investigation after ministers previously said the 24-year-old Polish attacker - who remains in a critical condition - was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies". A British national and Austrian woman were among those killed alongside four Poles. Professor Michal PÄdziwiatr and Dr Mateusz Wierdak were having lunch in central Krakow with their families when they heard gunshots, local media reported. "Suddenly my son ran up and said: 'Dad, they're shooting at people there, people are falling to the ground'," PÄdziwiatr told news outlet Fakt. PÄdziwiatr said when they got to the scene, they treated both the apparent attacker and the police officers. "When it comes to saving lives, it doesn't matter who is who," he added. Once the shooting stopped, PÄdziwiatr said he took care of the other victims and the perpetrator, while Wierdak began working on the police officer who was shot in the chest during the gunfight. "He, to put it colloquially, stuffed all the bandages into [the police officer's] chest and stuck his hands in," he told Fakt. "If not for that, I don't know how things would have turned out, as there was a long wait for the ambulance." Meanwhile, PÄdziwiatr said he called John Paul II Hospital where the Department of Thoracic and Cardiac Surgery is located. "I insisted they take him there because, in my opinion, he had the best chance of survival there, where there were specialists for precisely this type of injury," he told Fakt. According to local media, Wierdak is a renowned surgeon in Krakow. The University Hospital in Krakow states PÄdziwiatr is head of General, Oncological, Metabolic and Emergency Surgery. The police officers have been identified as senior constables Jakub Kulik and Artur MoraÅski. The attacker has not yet been named by authorities. When his house was searched after the attack in central Krakow, the bodies of his parents and sister were found. The National Public Prosecutor's Office in Poland launched an investigation into the attack with a unit specialising in "terrorist offences" taking the lead. Separately, reports emerged that six Dublin Civil Defence volunteers also assisted in the aftermath of the shooting. James McConnell, an officer, told RTE News the group were on a city break and were close to the main square, external when the shooting happened. The volunteers who are trained to provide medical care immediately sought to help injured people, providing "CPR and haemorrhage control". Witnesses who were close to the attack described panic and confusion around the square as it unfolded. Ruby Catherine Warren, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives". Not knowing where the gunman was - or if there was more than one - they "just kept sprinting", eventually finding a hotel to hide inside. Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover". "I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away," he said. The suspect wore full military tactical gear during the attack and was described as having a military-grade weapon - but the government said he was not a member of the Polish armed forces. Poland's Interior Minister Marcin KierwiÅski said "everything suggests" the suspect was "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held ultra-nationalist views. The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) on Saturday in the historic centre of Krakow. Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out. The glass fronts of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes. The mayor of Krakow said he had submitted an urgent request for the two officers injured while stopping the attacker to be awarded titles of honorary citizens of the city. Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted. - Published8 hours ago - Published9 hours ago - Published1 day ago - Published1 day ago
entry.summary: Further details have emerged about two police officers hailed for preventing a Polish gunman from killing more.

entry.title: Arrest made following shootings that killed 1 and injured 3 others on Winston-Salem State University campus - NBC News
entry.body: Authorities have made an arrest in connection to one of two shootings on Winston-Salem State University’s campus that killed one person and wounded three others Saturday. Ziyaire Antonyo Spinks, 20, was arrested in connection to a shooting that killed 19-year-old Peyton Izaia Patterson, Winston-Salem Police Department said in a statement Sunday. Spinks is facing charges of murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill inflicting serious injury, and felony possession of a firearm on an educational campus. Officers who responded after hearing shots fired found Patterson suffering from a gunshot wound. The officers and emergency medical services attempted life saving measures, police said, but he did not survive. The shooting injured Alyssa Janae Ellerbee, 19, who was treated at a hospital and later released, police said. Police have determined this shooting to be an isolated incident, not connected to a separate shooting that also occurred on campus Saturday night. Spinks is being held without bond, according to police. Court records show Spinks has two prior court cases pending in the state of North Carolina. He has a pending case in Randolph County involving a concealed weapon and marijuana possession charges from an arrest in March. The lawyer representing Spinks in the March case told NBC News Sunday that he was unaware of the new charges in Forsyth County. Spinks was indicted in October on charges of felony conspiracy to commit robbery and robbery with a dangerous weapon in Guilford County. The alleged offense occurred last year but the indictment was filed on Oct. 5, according to court records. The attorney representing him in Guilford County did not immediately respond to a NBC News request for comment. The shooting stemmed from an altercation between two groups, according to Jason Swaim, assistant chief of the Field Services Bureau for the Winston-Salem Police Department. An additional arrest was made against Cequon Warren Brower, 18, in connection to fighting. “One thing I’ll add about the homicide on campus — because I know this has been a question — is that the arrestee that’s been charged with murder, Mr. Spinks, he was not a student of Winston-Salem State University, and neither was Cequon Brower,” Swaim told reporters Sunday. That shooting occurred at 9:46 p.m. and another shooting was reported on campus at 10:22 p.m, Swaim said. Two people were found with gunshot wounds by the responding officers. A vehicle related to that incident was identified and later stopped by West Side police officers. No arrests have been made in that case as of Sunday afternoon, according to Swaim. Saturday was homecoming game day at the historically black university, with the WSSU Rams facing the Fayetteville State Broncos earlier in the day. Winston-Salem State University Police Chief Amir Henry assured the public that the campus was secured. He noted that this was typically a time for the university’s community to come together in “shared pride and connection.” “Tragically, this year, this celebration has been overshadowed by the loss of life and the injuries resulting from two separate shootings on our campus,” Henry said. Emergency services audio obtained by NBC News showed officers reporting one victim suffered a gunshot wound to the head. Another recording showed an officer calling for a second ambulance. Remaining homecoming activities scheduled for Sunday were canceled, including an event at the Emmanuel Baptist Church, according to a statement from Winston-Salem State University Chancellor Bonita J. Brown expressed her condolences to the family of the deceased victims and said she was praying for the recovery of those who were injured. She also acknowledged that members of the campus community “may have witnessed or experienced things that no one should have to endure.” She urged people to utilize the university’s counseling services and continue to follow police instructions as the investigation in the shootings continued. “Throughout our history, Winston-Salem State University has faced challenges, but we have always found strength in one another,” Brown wrote. “That is what it means to be part of the Ramily and to be Ram strong.”
entry.summary: Arrest made following shootings that killed 1 and injured 3 others on Winston-Salem State University campus NBC News See more headlines & perspectives on Google News

entry.title: Nvidia opens investigation after reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence - NBC News
entry.body: Nvidia’s board of directors said Sunday that it is opening an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The announcement followed reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who the newspapers reported had been recruited to spy for China. The two are not related. NBC News has not confirmed either report, and it has asked the Trump administration for comment. “The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company said in a statement. “A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.” The company added that while it “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” In a memo to Nvidia employees that the company shared with NBC News, Huang said: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.” The New York Times and the Financial Times reported that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen whose Singapore-based company was buying Nvidia’s advanced chips, had been under surveillance by U.S. Those agencies, the reports said, found that she had been recruited to spy by China’s top intelligence agency. Jensen Huang and Nvidia, for years, have been at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom. Nvidia’s products are the most highly sought-after chips in the world; however its top-tier products are mostly restricted from being sold to customers in China because of national security fears. China has long sought to become a global leader in AI. President Xi Jinping set a 2030 deadline to surpass the capabilities of American AI systems. Huang, 63, essentially serves as an ambassador for the industry, regularly appearing alongside the likes of President Donald Trump and King Charles III of Great Britain and at conferences to tout his company and what he says will be immense payoff in the future from AI. In October, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, one of the nation’s highest honors for achievement in science and technology. Nvidia is the world’s second-largest publicly traded company as of Friday, worth nearly $4.5 trillion. That’s up more than 500% over the last five years. But can they agree on AI? His net worth has soared from around $25 billion at the start of 2022 to almost $160 billion, making him the world’s 10th-richest person, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. But can they agree on AI? government about Alice Huang and Jensen Huang rose as high as Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Speaking Sunday to reporters in Florida shortly after Nvidia’s announcement, Rubio said, “I just can’t comment because of the nature of it, and I also can’t comment on an internal corporate matter that’s going on with Nvidia.” On Friday, the FT reported that the U.S. government believed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang. In response to the article, the FT reported that Nvidia declined to comment and said Jensen Huang meets “thousands of customer executives every year,” as any CEO normally does. Huang previously defended his interactions with Alice Huang, describing them as business-related in a recent statement: “Our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual.” In Sunday’s memo, Huang wrote: “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” The email to employees continued: “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.” A spokesperson for Nvidia told NBC News that “today’s news will not slow” the company and that Huang is “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.” Before Sunday’s announcement, Nvidia and Huang were already facing congressional scrutiny over the reports about Megaspeed and its executive. On Thursday, top House Republicans requested a briefing from Huang about the reports. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” said Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., who is also chairman of the House Select Committee on China. “PRC” is shorthand for the People’s Republic of China. “It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk,” a letter to Nvidia read.
entry.summary: Nvidia opens investigation after reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence NBC News Statement from NVIDIA Board of Directors NVIDIA Newsroom Nvidia CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy sparks security probe WCYB Nvidia launches investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over foreign intelligence concerns CNN Read Huang's email to his staff and statement from Nvidia's board of directors CNBC

entry.title: Top 5 stocks to watch this week - Yahoo Finance
entry.body: Investing.com -- Investors are preparing for a busy week on Wall Street, with earnings from five closely watched companies, fresh U.S. inflation data and shifting interest rate expectations likely to shape market sentiment. The NASDAQ Composite has entered correction territory, falling nearly 12% from its October 6 record, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq lost 2.7% and 3.4%, respectively, last week as technology stocks came under pressure and concerns over data-centre spending weighed on risk appetite. The earnings calendar also comes at a critical time for the technology sector, with investors also preparing for October U.S. Economists expect core consumer prices to rise 0.2% month over month, potentially lifting the annual rate to 2.7% from 2.6%. Producer price data due on Friday will provide another test for markets as traders assess the Federal Reserve's next policy move. Against this backdrop, five companies stand out this week, with their earnings and forward guidance likely to influence sentiment across the broader AI investment theme. Constellation Energy: Powering the AI infrastructure boom Constellation Energy will kick off the week's earnings calendar with results due before Monday's market open. The electricity producer has emerged as a key beneficiary of growing power demand from artificial intelligence data centres, making its outlook particularly important as investors assess the sustainability of infrastructure expansion. Its shares closed at $249.95 on November 6, down 30.2% year to date. Analysts expect earnings of $3.72 per share on revenue of $9.21 billion. The company has beaten earnings estimates by approximately 5.8% in each of its previous two quarters. Investors will focus on electricity demand, long-term supply agreements and management's assessment of data-centre power requirements. Any signs of political resistance to new infrastructure projects could also influence the outlook. CoreWeave: A crucial test for AI computing demand CoreWeave reports Tuesday after the market closes, with its results likely to provide one of the clearest indications of demand for AI computing infrastructure. The stock closed at $46.40 on November 6, down 43% over the past month and 59% over six months. Analysts expect earnings of 9 cents per share, although consensus estimates have been cut 12.6% over the past 90 days. The company's previous two earnings reports triggered sharply contrasting reactions. Shares fell 17.3% following a first-quarter earnings miss before gaining 22.2% after a second-quarter beat. Investors will closely examine capital expenditure, customer commitments and backlog commentary to determine whether demand for AI computing capacity remains strong enough to justify the industry's substantial infrastructure investments. Nebius Group: A gauge of investor appetite for neocloud stocks Nebius Group will report before the market opens on Thursday, offering another important assessment of sentiment toward specialised AI cloud infrastructure providers. Its shares closed at $129.49 on Friday, rising 7.6% during the session but remaining down 41% over the past month. The stock is still up 48.9% year to date. Nebius shares surged 32% following its second-quarter results and 23.5% after its first-quarter report, highlighting the market's sensitivity to developments in the AI infrastructure business. Investors will look for updates on capacity expansion, customer demand and financing arrangements as the company scales its operations. Its results could either reinforce or challenge the signals emerging from CoreWeave's report earlier in the week. Applied Materials: Testing the semiconductor spending outlook Applied Materials, a major supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, will report Thursday after the market closes. Its results could provide insight into whether chipmakers are maintaining investment plans despite growing concerns about AI spending. The stock closed at $332.72 on November 6, down 34.7% over the past month, although it remains up 44.6% over the past year. Analysts expect earnings of $4.06 per share on revenue of $10.30 billion. Notably, earnings estimates have risen 10.5% over the past 90 days, making Applied Materials one of the few companies on this week's watchlist where analyst expectations have strengthened despite a sharp share-price decline. Investors will assess orders, customer spending plans and management's guidance for semiconductor equipment demand to determine whether the sector's weakness reflects a temporary valuation reset or a slowdown in capital investment. Cisco Systems: AI networking demand in focus Cisco Systems will round out Thursday's earnings calendar with results due after the market closes. The networking equipment maker offers another perspective on the AI infrastructure buildout, particularly demand for networking products connecting increasingly complex data-centre systems. Its shares closed at $93.85 on November 6, down 18.3% over the past month. Analysts expect earnings of $1.32 per share on revenue of $18.11 billion, while earnings estimates have increased 15.4% over the past 90 days. Investors will scrutinise AI-related orders, networking demand and profit margins for evidence that the company's exposure to data-centre expansion is translating into stronger financial performance. Any disappointment in AI momentum or margins could intensify pressure on the stock, although improving earnings estimates suggest expectations may be more supportive than recent share-price weakness indicates. What investors should watch next The five earnings reports will provide an important snapshot of the AI investment cycle, spanning electricity supply, computing capacity, cloud infrastructure, semiconductor equipment and networking. The next major catalyst will be Nvidia's November 17 earnings report, which is expected to offer a broader assessment of demand across the AI ecosystem. Until then, investors will look to this week's results and management commentary for evidence that the industry's spending commitments remain intact despite mounting market concerns.
entry.summary: Top 5 stocks to watch this week Yahoo Finance US Inflation Set to Simmer Down Some After Recent Pickup Bloomberg Inflation, housing, jobs and corporate earnings will dominate the business calendar this week AP News Inflation Data, Constellation Energy, Skydance, Applied Materials, and More to Watch This Week Barron's Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: U.S. Inflation Data Could Give Clues on Rate-Hike Prospects WSJ

entry.title: Binance names new CFO days after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency hack - Fox Business
entry.body: Binance names new CFO days after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency hack Binance says its CFO succession plan was underway months before the $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft, as the exchange works to recover stolen assets and bolster security. Binance has named a new chief financial officer just over a week after hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from the exchange in what is believed to be the largest digital asset theft on record. Kaiser Ng is leaving the company after more than five years to pursue a new venture, Binance co-CEO He Yi said in a statement provided to FOX Business. Justin Yek, a former finance executive at global payments firm Airwallex, will succeed him. The announcement comes nine days after the Oct. 29 cyberattack, but a Binance spokesperson confirmed to FOX Business that the leadership transition was planned more than six months ago and had no connection to the security incident. BINANCE DETAILS HOW A FAKE JOB INTERVIEW LED TO A $6.3B CRYPTO HEIST "Kaiser Ng has decided to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance, with a transition plan implemented over the last half year," He Yi said. The CFO change comes as Binance works to recover stolen assets and strengthen its cybersecurity defenses following the attack, which the FBI has attributed to North Korean hackers associated with an operation known as "TraderTraitor." FRANCE BLOOD BANK CYBERATTACK TARGETS REFRIGERATION SYSTEMS AS EUROPEAN SUPERMARKETS HIT Binance has pledged to absorb the losses rather than pass them on to customers. Co-CEO Richard Teng previously told FOX Business that customers would not bear any losses and that the exchange had replenished affected assets. 3 update, Binance said it had replenished 98% of the affected token assets and that approximately $2.85 billion in stolen assets had been frozen or intercepted. The exchange also said it was working with law enforcement and industry partners to trace the stolen funds while bolstering its cybersecurity defenses. Binance said hackers used a fraudulent job interview to compromise an employee's computer before exploiting internal systems, including an artificial intelligence tool, to execute unauthorized cryptocurrency transactions. Ng had served as Binance's CFO since January 2022 and previously worked at rival cryptocurrency exchange Kraken. His successor, Yek, most recently served as Airwallex's vice president of finance. The payments company announced his appointment as head of strategic finance and corporate development in February 2023, noting his previous experience at Morgan Stanley and Citi. Yek said he was grateful for Ng's partnership during the transition over the past several months. CLICK HERE TO GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO "I look forward to leading our finance organization as we continue to scale responsibly and deliver on our mission globally," Yek told FOX Business. Reuters contributed to this report.
entry.summary: Binance names new CFO days after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency hack Fox Business Binance Says Kaiser Ng Leaving, Names Justin Yek New CFO Bloomberg North Korea's army of world-class hackers is secret weapon that took down Binance Reuters Insurers After $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist: D’oh! Gizmodo It Turns Out Binance’s $6 Billion Hack Happened Because Its Employees Were Vibe Coding Futurism

entry.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy
entry.body: Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation. Nvidia also published a message that Huang sent to the company admitting that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed (though he didn’t mention her by name). A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Jensen Huang wrote. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang added that he’d “fallen short” of his responsibility to the company. “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said. As the AI race between the United States and China heats up, chips, especially Nvidia’s chips, have been a major focus. Huang also seems to have a close relationship with President Donald Trump, who’s been a cheerleader of the AI (or “superintelligence”) industry. In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said that it has “no reason to believe” that either national security or company secrets were compromised. It also said that Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” and that the board has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” The investigation will be conducted by independent directors working with outside legal counsel. In response to earlier reports about the CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair’s interactions were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with customers. Other companies involved in the AI boom have warned employees to be wary of possible spies, including those offering sex or romance.
entry.summary: In a memo to the company, Huang admitted that he had an affair.

entry.title: Coordinated disturbances haunt grids worldwide. Here’s how researchers solved the mystery.
entry.body: For years, mysterious electrical anomalies have been flummoxing grid managers around the world. Every 60 seconds, the frequency on the grid would drop a tiny bit. Even weirder: The sags happened at the exact same time on power grids across countries and continents. It was a mystery that Dirk Witthaut, a researcher at Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany, couldn’t pass up. Germany’s largest transmission system operator, Tennet Germany, brought the puzzle to Witthaut, and it took years of investigative and modeling work to determine the cause. From Europe to Australia, the U.S. to Malaysia, the same pattern shows up in the data. Such frequency drops aren’t unheard of, but they are troubling. And the regularity with which they have been occurring can make the phenomenon feel even more ominous. Balancing the grid The grid’s orderly operation relies on the frequency being kept within a certain range. If the oscillations get get too large, or if grid operators don’t know the cause and respond improperly, they can lead to blackouts. Even if the sags don’t cause blackouts, they can damage equipment in power plants if they go unchecked, especially in hydropower turbines. Hydropower plants have historically been a main driver of so-called ultra-low frequency oscillations (UFLOs). Every turbine vibrates, and if those vibrations occur with a certain regularity, known as the resonant frequency, they can magnify, sometimes to dangerous levels. Think of a wine glass breaking before an opera singer’s mighty pipes — that’s resonance. So Witthaut and his team started investigating hydropower, the most obvious potential culprit. They used a computer model of a hydropower plant control system on the Scandinavian grid to test the hypothesis. While they managed to find conditions that could generate a resonance that peaked once per minute, they couldn’t explain why it persisted for so long. Typically, resonances in mechanical systems will come and go, and so will the accompanying signal on the electrical grid. But this frequency drop kept happening minute after minute after minute. Every 60 seconds, without fail. It then dawned on the team that anything operating with such clockwork required, well, a clock. How else could they explain the uncanny timing? Searching for clues To that hypothesis, the researchers started close to home, installing more than 80 smart power quality meters around the Jülich campus. The research site is outfitted with medium- and low-voltage distribution lines, transformers, solar panels, and battery energy storage systems that serve as uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). It also has a high-performance computer system as well as the usual office computers powered by much smaller UPS devices. The power quality meters sampled a range of attributes, including frequency, voltage, current, and power, once every three seconds. Before long, the research team had its answer. The measurements recorded on the transformer attached to the battery energy storage system peaked every minute, just like on the bigger power grids. It turns out that many stationary batteries, from data center UPSes to large grid-scale batteries, check their state-of-charge every minute. Since these devices are internet-connected, their clocks are in near perfect synchronicity. Every time one checks its charge, the disturbance is imperceptible on the wide grid. But when they all do it together, that disruption becomes apparent. To find evidence that UPSes were the main culprit on the grid, Witthaut and his team turned to data provided by grid operators. They found their answer in Ireland. There, data centers have grown to consume a large fraction of the country’s electricity. By 2022, data centers represented 18% of the load on Ireland’s grid, and each facility is served by a fleet of UPSes. Sure enough, between 2016 and 2021, the minute-by-minute frequency drop on the Irish grid quadrupled from 3 milli-Hertz (mHz) in 2016 to 12 mHz in 2021. More recently, some drops have exceeded 20 mHz. Ireland’s 50 Hz grid is built to withstand swings of plus or minus 200 mHz, though the grid operator would rather limit the swings to 100 mHz. In that range, 20 mHz isn’t a lot, but data centers aren’t the only loads on the grid. If other loads also cause the frequency to sag, the extra bump from every UPS checking its state-of-charge could push the grid toward blackout conditions. The solution The problem is entirely preventable. Rather than check state-of-charge exactly on the minute, Witthaus and team recommend that UPS and grid-scale battery manufacturers add some randomization to the schedule. While UPSes are driving the problem today, there’s a risk that the phenomenon could persist. The researchers also tested IoT devices. In devices as diverse as a smart oven and Raspberry Pi clusters, they were able to detect periodic power fluctuations. The fix is also a simple software patch, but many IoT devices go unpatched. A recent study found that less than 3% of IoT devices are running the latest firmware. Regulators may soon have to step in to demand changes, but they can only address their corner of the grid. Given the global nature of the issue, it’ll ultimately require global coordination. The mystery may be solved, but the problem could remain for years to come.
entry.summary: Mystery solved: Coordinated power drops have been haunting power grid worldwide, but a team of researchers in Germany found the culprit.

entry.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
entry.body: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it’s keeping pace with its rivals. Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic Future versions of Siri will be able to control third-party apps and perform more complex tasks. Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example. But that’s just the start. Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs. Gurman says: Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

entry.title: Epic Games Launcher is coming to SteamOS
entry.body: In October, Epic Games said that it was “investigating” making Fortnite compatible with Valve’s Linux-based SteamOS. At the time, Epic Games Launcher was in preview, but SteamOS was not specifically listed as a supported distro. Now, Communications Director Jake Jones has confirmed SteamOS compatibility, along with a handful of other distros, to GamingOnLinux. In response to a question about the AppImage being replaced with Debian / Ubuntu .deb downloads, Jones said: Epic Games Launcher is coming to SteamOS Epic Games confirmed that its Linux launcher will officially support SteamOS and Steam Decks. “The new Epic Games Launcher is still in Preview and we plan to support as many Linux distributions as possible, including Fedora, SteamOS, Cachy, Omarchy, and more. We’re testing and evaluating packaging formats for distribution, and we’ll restore AppImage this month.” That doesn’t necessarily mean Fortnite will come to SteamOS. Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) Linux v2 support still remains an open question. When it announced its work to bring Fortnite to Linux, the company said that the Steam Deck “does not support the required features for our EAC v2 solution, but we are actively talking with Valve and hope to support it in the future.”

entry.title: Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins Live Score and Stats - November 8, 2026 Gametracker - CBS Sports
entry.body: Lions push win streak to four with 19-9 victory over Dolphins MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. (AP) The Detroit Lions have repeated a mantra all week in the aftermath of a scary neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. They did that against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs had a rushing touchdown, Jared Goff threw for 170 yards and the Lions beat the Dolphins 19-9 for their fourth straight victory. “The whole week was prepare and play like Jack. Kind of felt like we owed it to him. It’s all we can do,” Detroit coach Dan Campbell said, adding later: “This was hard because you want to talk about it and acknowledge it. You don’t want to brush it under the rug. The guy means too much to us. We bonded together and ultimately we found a way to win the game. It was emotional.” Jake Bates made four field goals on a day that was a bit underwhelming for Goff and the Lions' top-ranked offense, which entered averaging 29 points and 395.4 yards per game but finished with 271 yards. Goff completed 17 of 25 passes while being sacked three times as Miami's defense pressured him throughout. Goff was intercepted by rookie cornerback Chris Johnson on a tipped pass in the first quarter - just the second pick he has thrown this season. Gibbs averaged just 3.7 yards per carry, finishing with 74 yards on 20 attempts and an 8-yard rushing score that put the Lions ahead 16-6 entering the fourth. Brown had 86 yards receiving for the Lions, who are trying to keep pace in a tough NFC North. Lions players arrived at Hard Rock Stadium wearing No. 46 jerseys to honor Jack Campbell, who was placed on injured reserve this week after he was hospitalized with the neck injury suffered during last Sunday's win over Minnesota. Campbell's jersey was hanging in his locker at the stadium before the game, and some fans raised signs that read “Campbell Strong.” “That’s a tough line you stand on - this balance beam of football and life and what really matters,” edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson said. “For us to come out today and get the win with all that in our head and think about him while we’re doing it, it’s really important.” The Lions never trailed but could not pull away from the rebuilding Dolphins, who had been in four consecutive one-score games entering Sunday. Bates made kicks of 28, 33, 40 and 43 yards. His 43-yarder gave Detroit a 10-point lead with 4:28 remaining. The Lions led 9-6 with four minutes left in the third when Goff connected with Jameson Williams for a 31-yard pickup - Detroit’s longest play of the game - that set up Gibbs' touchdown run on fourth down, his 11th scrimmage TD this season. Then the Dolphins took a page out Dan Campbell's book of aggressive play-calling, executing a fake punt that gave Miami the ball at Detroit's 18, setting up a 34-yard field goal by Zane Gonzalez. Malik Willis completed 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards and an interception while facing constant pressure from Detroit's front. Willis didn't use his legs as much as he has in previous games. He has a nagging groin injury and said after the game it “was a little tight.” The Dolphins went 0 for 3 in the red zone and failed to top 100 yards rushing for the second straight game. And despite staying within striking distance, the Dolphins had far too many self-inflicted wounds - including 11 penalties, a missed field goal and a kickoff that fell short of the landing zone. “We can’t keep saying the same things like, ‘Oh, we’ve got to get better,'” Willis said. “We've got to continue to fight to actually do it and make sure that shows up on game day.” Campbell picked up his 54th regular-season win as Detroit's coach, moving into second place alone in franchise history midway through his sixth season. Wayne Fontes is the Lions' winningest coach with 66 victories from 1988-96. Dolphins punter Bradley Pinion connected with Kaytron Allen for a 46-yard completion on Miami's fourth-quarter fake punt. It was a good job by them,” Dan Campbell said. “That certainly wasn’t on our guys. That was on me.” In the second quarter, Jack Fox lined up to punt before tossing an 11-yard pass to Tay Martin, which gave Detroit the ball at the 41. The Dolphins' defense held, though, sacking Goff on third down to force a real punt. “Why did we give up the fake punt? We've got to go look back and make sure we’re not giving anything away,” Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. “They clearly saw something on tape that they took advantage of, just like we saw something on tape and we took advantage of it.” Dolphins: TE Will Kacmarek (quad) was injured on a low hit in the third quarter. He remained down for a couple of minutes before walking to the sideline unassisted. Lions: Travel to Germany, where they will face New England in Munich next Sunday. entry.title: Denver Broncos vs. Carolina Panthers Live Score and Stats - November 8, 2026 Gametracker - CBS Sports
entry.body: Broncos top Panthers 26-21 for fifth straight win CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns and the Denver Broncos benefitted from a momentum-turning coach’s challenge to beat the Carolina Panthers 26-21 on Sunday for their fifth straight win. Jonah Coleman ran for 57 yards and a score and Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant each caught TD passes for the Broncos. Denver (7-2) got a late defensive stop as Nik Bonitto came up with a strip-sack on Bryce Young and recovered the ball near midfield with 1:24 left. The Broncos picked up one first down to seal the win. Young finished 28 of 39 for 276 yards with three touchdown passes and an interception for Carolina. He was sacked three times after being sacked six times in a loss last week to Green Bay. Darren Waller had eight catches for 90 yards and a touchdown for the Panthers (3-5), who have lost three straight. The Panthers took the lead early in the third quarter when Young found Waller over the middle for a 15-yard touchdown pass. The turning point came late in the third quarter when Broncos coach Sean Payton won a key challenge. With Carolina facing a first-and-goal at the Denver 1, Young threw a pass toward the corner of the end zone that was initially ruled incomplete. After the Panthers had run a second down play, officials stepped in and said Payton had thrown the red challenge flag before the snap. Upon review, officials ruled that Denver safety Devon Key had caught a ball that deflected off tight end Tommy Tremble's hand before it hit the ground. The interception gave the Broncos the ball at their 20 and ended Carolina's momentum and a chance to go up by eight. Denver took advantage, going 80 yards in 14 plays to take a 19-14 lead on a 9-yard touchdown run by Jonah Coleman with 10:17 remaining. Denver's 2-point conversion pass failed. Nix made it a two-possession game when he connected with a wide-open Bryant on a 25-yard touchdown pass down the seam with 5:41 left. Young cut the lead to five with a 4-yard TD pass to Tetairoa McMillan with 3:05 left and would get another chance after the Broncos lost 18 yards on a misplayed pitchout from Nix to Coleman and were forced to punt with two minutes left. But Bonitto's sack-fumble turned out to be the play of the game. The Panthers played their first game under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash, who replaced Ejiro Evero last week. But his defense, playing without its top four cornerbacks because of injuries, was flagged seven times, including five for pass interference. Denver: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss suffered concussions in the first half and were ruled out for the remainder of the game. Host Las Vegas on Nov. entry.title: Cowboys survive after wild CeeDee Lamb catch and fumble late in win over Colts - Yahoo Sports
entry.body: Luckily for the Dallas Cowboys, CeeDee Lamb's wild catch-turned-fumble late on Sunday afternoon didn't cost them the game at Lucas Oil Stadium. The Cowboys beat the Indianapolis Colts 27-23 after a game-winning touchdown from Javonte Williams in the final two minutes. But it was a sequence with Lamb earlier in the fourth quarter that could have cost them the contest. Lamb made an incredible catch in the fourth quarter and managed to complete the grab while just barely staying in bounds right up against the sideline. But instead of completing the play, Colts rookie cornerback Kenneth Harris didn't actually touch Lamb. So Lamb jumped up and ended up with a 48-yard play, deep into Colts territory. But as Lamb was tackled, he actually lost the ball going down. That gave the ball right back to Indianapolis after a review. It looked like that was going to cost Dallas the game, too. The Colts made it all the way down into scoring position, thanks to three major penalties — including a 40-yard pass interference call on DaRon Bland. But inside the red zone, Quinnen Williams forced a huge fumble to give Dallas the ball right back and stop what could have been a go-ahead touchdown drive. Eventually, it was Williams' touchdown that pushed Dallas ahead for good and gave it the four-point win. Dak Prescott went 21-of-34 for 335 yards with two touchdowns in the win, which pushed the Cowboys to 4-5 on the season. They are second in the NFC East race, behind only the New York Giants. Lamb had 195 yards and a touchdown on 10 catches. He found the end zone in the second quarter on a 44-yard catch. The Cowboys will take on the San Francisco 49ers next week.

entry.title: Norris wins gripping race after Antonelli and Russell errors
entry.body: Norris wins gripping race after Antonelli and Russell errors - Published McLaren's Lando Norris beat Max Verstappen to win a gripping Sao Paulo Grand Prix in which new world champion Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes team-mate George Russell both made critical mistakes in difficult conditions. Norris, who started from pole, lost the lead to Antonelli at the start and dropped back when the track was wet. But an earlier pit stop for dry-weather tyres put Norris on Antonelli's tail and the Italian spun away the lead at the first corner. After reclaiming first place, Norris dominated through a late shower of rain which required a switch back to wet-weather tyres to take his first win since the Dutch Grand Prix at the end of August. A few laps before Antonelli lost the lead, Russell, who started seventh, spun exiting the pits and lost 15 to 20 seconds after working his way back into podium contention. Despite their travails, Russell and Antonelli finished fourth and fifth to clinch the constructors' championship for Mercedes a week after the Italian had tied up the drivers' title. Norris had too much pace for Verstappen whether the track was dry or wet and stamped his authority on the race. But the Dutchman put in another supreme drive in changeable conditions in Interlagos to take second after starting in 21st place. The key stories of the race were: - An accomplished performance from Norris in a revived McLaren to take his first win for more than two months - A superb comeback from Verstappen from an engine penalty - A difficult day for both Mercedes, notwithstanding the greater glory of the constructors' win, and Ferrari in the tricky conditions - Norris brilliant in wet & Verstappen recovery extraordinary - driver ratings - Published1 hour ago Norris had started from his first pole position since the Spanish Grand Prix in September, but lost first place immediately after Antonelli, alongside him on the front row, leaped into the lead. The new world champion pulled away to build a five-second advantage in 10 laps as he began to look as if he might crown his achievement with a win at the first attempt. Antonelli's lead was more than eight seconds by lap 13 but the track was drying and three laps later Norris came in for dry-weather slick tyres. The Italian followed him in a lap later, but Norris had gained so much time with his earlier stop that he was on the Mercedes' gearbox when it rejoined. Antonelli defended for a couple of laps but he was complaining over the radio that the car felt strange under acceleration, and on lap 20 he lost control on the entry to Turn One, spinning and handing the lead to Norris. That left Norris three seconds ahead of Hadjar with Verstappen now close behind Antonelli, who ran wide again at Turn One four laps later and handed third place to the Dutchman. Hadjar had every bit as much pace as Verstappen, but was not as consistent and made too many mistakes, and within 10 laps the team leader was on the Frenchman's tail. Red Bull ordered Hadjar to let Verstappen by on lap 39 in the hope the four-time champion could close on Norris. But the Briton had too much pace and held off Verstappen, switching to another set of soft tyres before needing intermediates when the rain came down increasingly heavily in the final 10 laps. Norris said: "It was a very tough race - very, very tough. Not the best of launches off the line, but a lot of challenges today with the conditions and going on slicks in the wet is always tough. "The main thing today was that I just kept it cool and I did not make any mistakes. I had the pace when I needed to so it was good. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well." Verstappen had made speedy progress up from his position at the back. Initially, Lewis Hamilton, who had started alongside the Red Bull, progressed faster, and was ninth by lap two, but Verstappen soon got into his stride and passed the Ferrari within a further two laps and continued his forward progress. By lap 10, Verstappen was up to a remarkable sixth place and right behind the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson, with Hadjar ahead chasing Russell, who by then was up to third after starting seventh. But Russell dashed his own hopes when he stopped on lap 16, at the same time as Norris, and spun in the pit lane exit which mirrors on the inside of the track the run through the Senna S first two corners. Russell was broadside in the pit lane as rivals squeezed past him left and right as he manoeuvred his way straight again and rejoined the race, now down in 10th. After that, he drove well with strong pace to put himself back in contention and a fourth-place finish was a strong result in the circumstances. He had more pace than Antonelli in the closing laps and the team ordered them to swap positions as they sealed their ninth constructors' title, and first since 2021. Both Antonelli and and Charles Leclerc were handed five-second time penalties by the stewards for separate incidents after the race. The penalty for an unsafe release does not affect Antonelli's fifth-place finish, but Ferrari's Leclerc drops to eighth for causing a collision late on with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson, who is promoted to seventh. McLaren's Oscar Piastri was sixth, nowhere near Norris' pace, while Hamilton took ninth. After his initial burst up the field, the seven-time champion lacked pace, despite pushing correctly for an early stop for slicks, and could make no more ground. Although leading Leclerc for much of the race, Hamilton fell behind him with his second stop for slicks, while Leclerc hung on for the change to intermediates to consolidate his position. Audi's Nico Hulkenberg took the final point for 10th place. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) 3. Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) 4. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) 8. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) What's next? The season is due to end with a final triple header, starting with the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The night race is due to start at 04:00 GMT on Sunday, 22 November. Related topics - Published2 days ago

entry.title: Norris brilliant in wet & Verstappen recovery extraordinary - driver ratings
entry.body: Norris brilliant in wet & Verstappen recovery extraordinary - driver ratings - Published McLaren's Lando Norris secured his third win of the season on Sunday by beating Max Verstappen to victory at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Norris started on pole position but lost the lead of the wet-dry-wet race to new world champion Kimi Antonelli on the opening lap. But after an early pit stop for dry tyres, he regained control when Mercedes' Antonelli spun at the first corner. Verstappen, meanwhile, claimed his eighth consecutive podium with another eye-catching drive in tricky conditions at Interlagos, while his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar finished third. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Brazil. Lando Norris - 10/10 Pretty difficult to ask for much more for the McLaren driver. Fastest in first practice on Friday, brilliant in the wet to take pole and then kept his head through constantly changing conditions to win comfortably. Losing the lead at the start was only a minor blemish. Max Verstappen - 9.5/10 Another extraordinary recovery drive in the Red Bull. Fastest in final practice and then charged from 21st to second, making up 10 places almost immediately, and once again looking completely at home in difficult conditions. Isack Hadjar - 9/10 One of his strongest weekends all season. Qualified well, ran with team-mate Verstappen for much of the race and delivered another podium despite a few mistakes along the way. Had the pace to make Red Bull think before eventually letting Verstappen through. George Russell - 7.5/10 The pace was excellent all weekend and second in qualifying showed what was possible, even if his engine penalty dropped him to seventh. Spinning his Mercedes on the pit exit was a huge error and probably cost him a podium, but recovering to fourth was a very strong response. Kimi Antonelli - 6.5/10 For the opening stint this looked like the perfect first race as world champion. A brilliant start and built a healthy lead, but spinning it away after switching to the slick tyres unlocked a messy afternoon. Oscar Piastri - 6/10 Another weekend where things never really clicked. His qualifying result was compromised by the timing of the red flag, but he was a long way from Norris' pace in the race and finished almost a minute behind his McLaren team-mate. Liam Lawson - 8.5/10 An excellent weekend in the Racing Bulls. Qualified fifth, started third and even ran second during the opening stages before eventually slipping backwards as the race developed. Charles Leclerc - 6.5/10 A very good recovery from 14th on the grid after his power-unit penalty. Qualified fourth on pure pace and worked his way through to eighth. He passed Lawson towards the end but was given a five-second penalty for hitting the New Zealander, which means he finishes behind him. Lewis Hamilton - 6.5/10 The opening few laps were vintage Hamilton as he charged from 20th to ninth, but the progress then stalled. He struggled for pace in the Ferrari on the intermediate tyres, and a late spin capped a race where more looked possible after such a promising start. Nico Hulkenberg - 7.5/10 Outstanding in the wet qualifying session to put Audi sixth before penalties promoted him to fourth. A 10-second time penalty for going off track in his battle with Franco Colapinto hurt his Sunday, but he still came away with the final point. - Norris wins gripping race after Antonelli and Russell errors - Published49 minutes ago Arvid Lindblad - 7/10 His qualifying was cut short by a mechanical problem in his Racing Bulls and further power-unit changes left him starting well down the order. Recovered well to 11th and came extremely close to points. Fernando Alonso - 8/10 Reaching Q3 for the first time this season was a big positive and he raced well enough to even get ahead of Hamilton with a spectacular move in the Aston Martin. P12 doesn't look spectacular, but there was plenty to like about the weekend. Franco Colapinto - 6.5/10 Alpine struggled badly in the wet qualifying session but Colapinto made a reasonable recovery. Finished ahead of team-mate Pierre Gasly and was involved in the battle with Hulkenberg that eventually earned the Audi driver a penalty. Pierre Gasly - 5.5/10 A disappointing weekend after both Alpines went out in Q1. Made a little progress from 16th on the grid but finished behind Colapinto and never really threatened the points. Alex Albon - 7/10 Saturday was the highlight after reaching Q3 for the first time this season and earning ninth on the grid. Unfortunately the race went the opposite way and he fell back to 15th in the Williams. Gabriel Bortoleto - 5/10 Showed good speed before qualifying but his crash in the Audi in Q1 put him on the back foot for his home race. Oliver Bearman - 5.5/10 A really strong Saturday to put the Haas eighth in qualifying and sixth on the grid. The race was a completely different story, though, as he tumbled out of contention and eventually finished 17th. Sergio Perez - 5/10 Starting last because of his engine penalty made it difficult from the outset. Kept his nose clean, picked up several positions in his Cadillac and reached the finish ahead of a Williams and a Haas. Carlos Sainz - 4.5/10 Unlucky to have his Q2 attempt interrupted by the red flag just as he switched to the intermediates, but Sunday offered little recovery. Rafael Camara - 5.5/10 Plenty of raw speed on his F1 debut in the Haas but plenty of learning too. Reaching Q2 in those conditions was impressive, although two qualifying incidents and a difficult race ultimately left him 20th. Lance Stroll - 4/10 Out in Q1 and never looked capable of matching Aston Martin team-mate Alonso across the weekend. Valtteri Bottas - 4.5/10 Only 20th in qualifying before being promoted a couple of places on the grid. His race was over before it had even begun, with Cadillac retiring his car with a technical problem, so Sunday itself is impossible to judge. Related topics - Published2 days ago

entry.title: Falkirk add goals and grit to McGlynn's guile on rapid rise
entry.body: Falkirk add goals and grit to McGlynn's guile on rapid rise - Published In the space of a week Falkirk have beaten defending champions Celtic and become the first team to get the better of Hearts in a Scottish Premiership match at Tynecastle in 19 months, scoring a combined seven goals in the process. The 5-2 success in Edinburgh was their fifth successive victory and takes John McGlynn's side up to third place. A month ago, the concession of an added time goal to Dundee left them 11th, only a point off the bottom of the table. "It's striking a balance without getting carried away and not playing it down too much," McGlynn told BBC Scotland. "Winning five games in a row, you've obviously got something about you. We want it to continue because we're enjoying this. "But we're only 13 games in. There's a long way to go, so we've got to keep our feet on the ground and enjoy seeing our team third in the league." The 64-year-old earned plaudits aplenty last season for guiding Falkirk to sixth on their return to the top flight after overseeing consecutive promotions. Liam Henderson, who scored the sublime fourth goal against Hearts, was with the Bairns in those League One days, as were Brad Spencer and Ethan Ross. Unused substitutes Finn Yeats and Ross MacIver have been on the journey with McGlynn too, as has Leon McCann, who missed out through injury. "We've got a good team spirit, a togetherness, and a will to work hard for your team-mates," said centre-half Henderson. "We now have a ruthlessness up front as well. "The manager is massive to us. He is so detailed in everything he does. "We're breaking records this season and creating some history. A lot of pundits and fans were saying that we weren't the team we were last year." There is truth to that. While some of the old guard remain, there was a huge squad turnover in the summer. Calvin Miller went to Hearts, Dylan Tait is now the skipper at Dundee United and Barney Stewart, who scored 10 goals between January and May, was sold to West Bromwich Albion for a club record fee. Loan players Filip Lissah, Ben Broggio, Henry Cartwright, Kyrell Wilson, Ethan Williams and Louie Marsh said their goodbyes. McGlynn brought in a whopping 17 new faces, with Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames and Jacob Murrell, who all scored against Hearts, arriving weeks after the campaign had kicked off. Murrell, 22, picked up the SPFL player of the month award for October and his Tynecastle double takes his tally to seven, making him joint-top scorer in the division. "They look at what kind of player fits into the team and when the player arrives, they know what they're getting," said former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart in praise of Falkirk's scouting. Meanwhile, former Hibs midfielder Scott Allan highlighted captain Spencer as the "heartbeat" of the team. "You need a guy like him in there to really set the standards," Allan said of the 30-year-old midfielder, who followed McGlynn from Raith Rovers. "When he is in the team, there is a real control from Falkirk, especially in the middle. "They've added a steeliness to the team too, it's not always total football this year. They are able to do the dirty side of the game now and roll up the sleeves when they have to." McGlynn is very much the unassuming star of the show though. "He is a manager who is totally comfortable in his own skin now," said Stewart. Perhaps before he was considered a bit of an unfashionable manager. I mean in terms of stature, and not in what he's doing on the park. "The perception of him continues to get better and better. "I don't want to be disrespectful to Falkirk, but I would not be surprised, if, when one or two of the bigger jobs start coming up, rather than being an outsider, I think he will be right in the hunt for some of those." As things stand, almost any move away from Falkirk would be a step down the league.
entry.summary: Falkirk continue to excel under the canny guidance of John McGlynn as a run of five successive victories takes them up to third in the Scottish Premiership.

entry.title: Del Casher, Guitarist Who Invented the Wah-Wah Pedal, Dead at 88
entry.body: Del Casher, Guitarist Who Invented the Wah-Wah Pedal, Dead at 88 Del Casher, the guitarist and inventor whose innovations included the wah-wah pedal, has died at the age of 88. Casher died October 1 following a battle with cancer, according to a GoFundMe to raise money for his widow Eiko. TMZ was first to report on Casher’s death. Born Delton Kacher in Hammond, Indana, Casher first performed with artists like Gene Autry, Lawrence Welk and the Three Suns while also experimenting with new techniques and technologies in an effort to make his own electric guitar playing stand out. In the early Sixties, while playing with the Thomas Organ company’s Vox Ampliphonic Orchestra, Casher asked about making his guitar sound like the trumpet, complete with the ability to mildly suppress the instrument mid-playing. While Casher often credited Thomas Organ’s Brad Plunkett as the engineer of the device, the wah-wah pedal was considered Casher’s brainchild. First dubbed the “Cry Baby” pedal, Casher also recorded a demo for instrument stores showcasing how to use the pedal, as well as an accompanying single. Both the pedal and the single failed to catch on with the music-playing public upon release in 1967. However, Frank Zappa, who used the wah-wah pedal in 1966 when Casher sat in with the Mothers of Invention, gifted a pedal to Jimi Hendrix, solidifying the wah-wah’s place in music history soon after. Hendrix would employ the pedal throughout his classic Electric Ladyland — including on “Voodoo Child,” “Burning of the Midnight Lamp,” and “All Along the Watchtower” — while fellow guitarist Eric Clapton wah-wah’d on Cream tracks like “Tales of Brave Ulysses.” Soon after, many of the great rock guitarists of the era, like Jimmy Page, Tony Iommi, David Gilmour, and more, were experimenting with the wah-wah pedal. By 1971, the wah-wah pedal had featured on a Number One single and Oscar-winning song thanks to its use on Isaac Hayes’ “Theme From Shaft.” Generations of guitar players have used the pedal since. Outside of inventing — Casher is also credited with contributing to the creation of the Ecco-Fonic and the Fender Electronic Echo Chamber — the guitarist also found work with artists like Elvis Presley, appearing in his 1964 film Roustabout. Casher also contributed film scores later in his career. “I feel gratified that I was there at the beginning,” Casher told the New York Times. “I would just like guitar players to think of me once in a while. The only thing I ask is: remember me.”
entry.summary: Musician and inventor who played with artists like Elvis Presley, Gene Autry and Frank Zappa died October 1 after cancer battle

entry.title: Dave Chappelle’s Charlie Kirk Joke Prompts Response from Erika Kirk: Using the ‘Destruction of a Human Life’ as a ‘Punchline Is Beyond Disgusting’
entry.body: After Dave Chappelle joked that he feels better ever since Charlie Kirk was murdered, Kirk’s widow, Erika, has responded to those using her late husband’s death as a punchline. “To see leftist podcasters, comedians, and commentators laugh about political assassination as though it’s entertainment and the destruction of a human life is a punchline, is beyond disgusting,” she wrote on X Sunday. “My husband, Charlie Kirk, was killed in an act of political violence, something our two children and I will live with every day for the rest of our lives.” She continued: “A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together. You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard. Political violence must never be something this country tolerates, excuses, or celebrates.” Chappelle has been receiving backlash across social media after footage from his Friday show at Madison Square Garden — which was advertised as a phone-free experience that would require devices be stored away in Yondr pouches – showed the comedian quipping about Kirk’s death. “I feel fucked up saying this. It’s scary being a public speaker,” Chappelle said. “Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but I feel better.” He continued: “I know I shouldn’t say that, but it’s just a feeling. I didn’t ask to feel this way…I just be driving around like, ‘Why am I in such a good mood? Oh!’” “I’ve Had It” podcast hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan also came under fire recently for laughing at a joke about Kirk during a Thursday episode of their show. The two released a joint statement on Saturday, writing that they “regret it” and “apologize.” The conservative activist and Turning Point USA co-founder died on Sept. 10, 2025, after being shot during a college event in Utah.

entry.title: Maya Jama Exits ‘Love Island U.K.’ as Host After 9 Seasons: ‘All Good Things Must Come to an End’
entry.body: “Love Island U.K.” host Maya Jama is exiting the dating series after nine seasons. Jama made the announcement on her Instagram account Sunday. “What an incredible era and what an unforgettable time I’ve had, it’s been far too much fun to put into words or a video,” she began her statement. “But as all good things must come to an end, it’s my time to step down as the host of my beloved Love Island.” She continued: “I’ve always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then, and now is my time to throw myself into something new.” Jama first joined as the show’s host in 2023, succeeding host Laura Whitmore. In the time since, her star has soared – Jama even competed on the recent second season of “Celebrity Traitors,” on which she was the only original Traitor to make it to the final episode. This year, Jama made her acting debut in the second season of Guy Ritchie’s critically acclaimed “The Gentlemen.” Before becoming a sought-after presenter, Jama made a name for herself as one of the youngest BBC Radio One DJs ever. Read her full statement here: What an incredible era and what an unforgettable time I’ve had, it’s been far too much fun to put into words or a video..but as all good things must come to an end, it’s my time to step down as the host of my beloved Love Island. Firstly, I want to thank all of the people who rooted so hard for me to host the show in the first place. I wouldn’t change a thing. To the fans of the show, thank you for every supportive message and every single time you’ve tuned in during my time as host, I’m forever grateful to you all. The show really does belong to the people who watch it and embrace it year after year. Biggest thanks to the incredible production team, I’ve seen firsthand how you work your asses off for months every year to bring this iconic show to life. I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the 9 incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I’ve loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show. I’ll forever be grateful for the experience. But I’ve always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then, and now is my time to throw myself into something new. While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I’ll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever.
